# The nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality and original-data rigidity

{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove the spacetime Penrose Inequality for smooth three-dimensional initial-data exteriors with one spherical asymptotically anti-de Sitter end, satisfying the stated decay and integrability assumptions, the dominant energy condition, and a compact weakly future outer trapped boundary. We assume that the hyperbolic metric four-flux is future timelike; its Lorentz norm is the mass, and the area is the infimum over full enclosing cuts. On the connected outermost, outer area-minimizing horizon subclass, equality characterizes the original data as a spacelike hypersurface in Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter spacetime with matching metric mass. No maximality, evolution, or auxiliary solvability assumption is used.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove the spacetime Penrose Inequality for smooth three-dimensional initial-data exteriors with one spherical asymptotically anti-de Sitter end, satisfying the stated decay and integrability assumptions, the dominant energy condition, and a compact weakly future outer trapped boundary. We assume that the hyperbolic metric four-flux is future timelike; its Lorentz norm is the mass, and the area is the infimum over full enclosing cuts. On the connected outermost, outer area-minimizing horizon subclass, equality characterizes the original data as a spacelike hypersurface in Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter spacetime with matching metric mass. No maximality, evolution, or auxiliary solvability assumption is used.

- **claim-sharp-invariant-penrose** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-main-numerical)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ satisfy Definition <a href="#def:setup-data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:setup-data">3</a>, the same future boundary condition $H+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{TS}K\le0$ on every component, and the future-timelike metric mass condition in Definition <a href="#def:setup-mass" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:setup-mass">5</a>. Then $$\label{eq:main-penrose} m_{\mathrm{AH}}(g)\ge \sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S)}{16\pi}} \left(1+\frac{A_{\min}(S)}{4\pi}\right) =\frac{r_A+r_A^3}{2}.$$ The coefficient is sharp. No maximality assumption, restriction on the compact topology or boundary genera, or outermostness hypothesis is required.
  - Explanation: Bounds the Lorentz norm of the metric mass covector by the full enclosing-area infimum, with sharp coefficient and without maximality or outermostness.
- **claim-original-data-equality** (classification, [source](#stmt-thm-main-rigidity)): Assume in addition the connected horizon hypotheses of Definition <a href="#def:setup-horizon" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:setup-horizon">8</a>. Equality in Equation <a href="#eq:main-penrose" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:main-penrose">[eq:main-penrose]</a> holds if and only if the original pair $(g,K)$ is realized by a smooth proper spacelike embedding of $\Omega$, with boundary, into the smooth maximally extended Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter spacetime of parameter exactly $M=m_{\mathrm{AH}}(g)$. Its interior lies in one black-hole exterior; its boundary maps diffeomorphically onto a full smooth spacelike cross-section of that exterior’s future event horizon, with the bifurcation sphere also allowed; and its unique end reaches that exterior’s conformal infinity. The embedding induces both $g$ and $K$ with the future-normal convention of Equation <a href="#eq:setup-expansion" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:setup-expansion">[eq:setup-expansion]</a>.
  - Explanation: Characterizes equality on the connected horizon subclass by a proper spacelike embedding inducing both original tensors and matching the actual metric mass.
- **claim-flux-convergence-covariance** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-setup-mass-covariance)): The decay and integrability in Definition <a href="#def:setup-data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:setup-data">3</a> imply convergence of the four integrals in Equation <a href="#eq:setup-flux" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq:setup-flux">[eq:setup-flux]</a>. The same limits are obtained on any smooth exhaustion whose boundary escapes every compact set. Under a fixed hyperbolic background isometry the covector $p$ transforms by the corresponding Lorentz transformation. It is invariant, with this transformation understood, under admissible asymptotic spatial chart changes: both charts must satisfy the tensor-decay and weighted-integrability conditions of Definition <a href="#def:setup-data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:setup-data">3</a>. In particular, a future-timelike $p$ can be balanced by a spatial change of hyperbolic chart so that $(p_0,p_1,p_2,p_3)=(m_{\mathrm{AH}},0,0,0)$.
  - Explanation: Establishes convergence, exhaustion independence, admissible spatial covariance, and balancing of a future-timelike metric mass covector.
- **claim-model-mass-normalization** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-setup-model-mass)): For $M>0$, let $F_M(r)=1+r^2-2M/r$ and let $r_h$ be its positive root. The metric $g_M=F_M^{-1}dr^2+r^2\sigma$ on $[r_h,\infty)$, with its smooth minimal-boundary interpretation, has $(p_0,p_1,p_2,p_3)=(M,0,0,0)$. A full smooth spacelike cross-section of the future horizon in the regular extension of $$\label{eq:setup-model-spacetime} \overline g_M=-F_M\,dt^2+F_M^{-1}dr^2+r^2\sigma$$ has area $4\pi r_h^2$, and $M=(r_h+r_h^3)/2$.
  - Explanation: Computes the model metric mass and the area of a full future-horizon section, fixing the normalization of the sharp bound.
- **claim-one-sign-component-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-str-one-sign)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ satisfy Definition <a href="#def:setup-data" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:setup-data">3</a>, and assume $H+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{TS}K\le0$ on every component of $S$, with the convention of Equation <a href="#eq:setup-expansion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setup-expansion">[eq:setup-expansion]</a>. Suppose that $K$ is compactly supported and that one of the two tensors $$K-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g,\qquad -K+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g$$ is positive semidefinite throughout $\Omega$. In each fixed admissible hyperbolic chart for which the metric fluxes exist, $$p_0(g)\geq \sqrt{\frac{A_g(S)}{16\pi}} +\frac12\left(\frac{A_g(S)}{4\pi}\right)^{3/2}. \label{eq:str-component-bound}$$ This assertion does not require the flux covector to be timelike. If that covector is future timelike, its Lorentz norm satisfies the same lower bound.
  - Explanation: Proves the component bound for compactly supported second fundamental form with a global stress sign, then obtains the invariant version when the covector is future timelike.
- **claim-one-sign-preparation** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-str-preparation)): Under the hypotheses of Theorem <a href="#thm:str-one-sign" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:str-one-sign">10</a>, there are smooth data $(g_i,K_i)$ on the same exterior, numbers $c_i>0$, and a fixed $0<\delta<1$ such that:* 1. *$K_i$ is compactly supported, with the same global stress sign as $K$, and its future boundary expansion has the original weak sign;* 2. *$\mathcal H_{g_i}(K_i)-2\|\mathcal J_{g_i}(K_i)\|_{g_i} \geq c_i(1+r)^{-3-\delta}$, with $r$ smoothly extended over a compact region;* 3. *$g_i=e^{4v_i}b$ on an exact tail, where $$v_i=r^{-3}v_{3,i}(\omega)-d_{0,i}r^{-3-\delta} +O_\infty(r^{-4}), \qquad d_{0,i}>0, \label{eq:str-prepared-expansion}$$ and $v_{3,i}$ is smooth;* 4. *for a fixed $\beta>3/2$, $g_i\to g$ and $K_i\to K$ in physical weighted $C^{2,\alpha'}_\beta$ and $C^{1,\alpha'}_\beta$ norms, respectively, with any fixed sufficiently small $\alpha'>0$;* 5. *$p_a(g_i)\to p_a(g)$ for all four metric fluxes and $A_{g_i}(S)\to A_g(S)$.* *When $K=0$, one may take $K_i=0$. A minimal boundary remains minimal, and the convergence on fixed compact subsets is smooth if the original metric is smooth there.
  - Explanation: Produces strict prepared data preserving the stress sign and boundary sign, with convergent cut infima and metric fluxes.
- **claim-short-collar-area-control** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-str-added-collar)): Let $(\Omega,g)$ be smooth up to its compact boundary. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ there is an enlarged exterior $(\Omega_\varepsilon,g_\varepsilon)$, obtained by adding a collar on the inner side of every boundary component, which agrees with $g$ on $\Omega$, has a product metric near its new boundary, and satisfies $$A_{g_\varepsilon}(\partial\Omega_\varepsilon) \geq(1-o(1))A_g(S)\qquad(\varepsilon\downarrow0). \label{eq:str-collar-area}$$ No constraint inequality on the added collar is required.
  - Explanation: Adds product boundary collars while controlling the full enclosing-area infimum; the auxiliary collars require no constraint inequality.
- **claim-fixed-height-stress-potential** (construction, [source](#stmt-str-pde-fixed-height)): Let $(X,g)$ be a connected smooth complete three-dimensional exterior with compact smooth nonempty boundary, exactly one end, and a smooth metric up to its boundary. Let $H_{\partial X}\leq0$, for the normal pointing into $X$. Suppose that on the end, with $z=r^{-1}$, $$\label{str-pde-prepared-end} g=z^{-2}\bar g,\qquad \bar g=e^{4v}\left(\frac{dz^2}{1+z^2}+\sigma\right),\qquad v=z^3v_3(\omega)-d z^{3+\delta}+O_\infty(z^4),$$ where $v_3$ is smooth, $0<\delta<1$, and the remainder and its tangential derivatives satisfy the indicated symbol estimates. For every $D>0$ there is a unique bounded weak solution $$\label{str-pde-dirichlet} \mathop{\mathrm{div}}_g\left(t(\|df\|_g)\frac{\nabla_g f}{\|df\|_g}\right)=0, \qquad f\|_{\partial X}=D,\qquad \lim_{r\to\infty}f=0.$$ It satisfies $0<f<D$ in the interior, has bounded physical gradient, belongs to $C^{1,\theta}$ on compact subsets including the finite boundary for some $\theta>0$, and is smooth wherever $df\ne0$. On a collar of conformal infinity it is noncritical and $$\label{str-pde-end-expansion} \begin{gathered} f=z C_f(\omega)+R_f,\qquad C_f\in C^\infty(\mathbb S^2), \qquad C_f>0,\\ \|(z\partial_z)^j\partial_\omega^\nu R_f\| \leq C_{j,\nu}z^2\quad(0\leq j\leq2). \end{gathered}$$ The constants can depend on $D$ and the fixed geometry. In particular, $$\label{str-pde-end-flux} \begin{gathered} \|df\|_g=zC_f+O(z^2),\qquad t(\|df\|_g)=z^2C_f^2+O(z^3),\\ -\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{\{r=\mathrm{const}\}} t(\|df\|_g)\left\langle\frac{\nabla_g f}{\|df\|_g},\nu_g\right\rangle dA_g=\int_{\mathbb S^2}C_f^2\,dA_\sigma . \end{gathered}$$
  - Explanation: Obtains the unique bounded stress potential with finite-boundary regularity, a noncritical conformal collar, and a positive smooth angular leading coefficient.
- **claim-stress-regularization-structure** (bound, [source](#stmt-str-pde-regularity-input)): For sufficiently small $h>0$, choose a smooth $b_h$ equal to $1$ on $[0,h/2]$, equal to $b$ on $[2h,\infty)$, and between $1$ and $2$ on the intervening interval. Define $t_h$ by $s t_h'/t_h=b_h$ and $t_h(2h)=t(2h)$. For each fixed $M<\infty$, $$\label{str-pde-regularized-structure} c_M(h+s)s\leq t_h(s)\leq C_M(h+s)s,\qquad c_M(h+s)\leq t_h'(s)\leq C_M(h+s) \quad(0\leq s\leq M).$$ Here $t_h(s)/s$ is constant near zero, so the regularized vector field is smooth at the zero covector. On coordinate patches with uniformly controlled metric and first derivatives, its density $$A_h^i(x,p)=\sqrt{\det g}\,\frac{t_h(\|p\|_g)}{\|p\|_g}g^{ij}p_j$$ obeys, for $\|p\|\leq M$, $$\label{str-pde-density-structure} \begin{split} \lambda_M(h^2+\|p\|^2)^{1/2}\|\zeta\|^2 &\leq D_pA_h[\zeta,\zeta],\qquad \|D_pA_h\|\leq\Lambda_M(h^2+\|p\|^2)^{1/2},\\ \|A_h\|+\|\partial_x A_h\|&\leq C_M(h+\|p\|)\|p\|. \end{split}$$ Once an a priori gradient bound $M$ has been established, the field can be extended for $\|p\|>M$ to satisfy these inequalities globally, with possibly changed constants independent of $h$.* *Consequently bounded weak solutions with this gradient bound have local $C^{1,\theta}$ estimates, including Dirichlet boundary patches, uniformly in $h$. On interior unit patches for $h=0$, the estimate can be normalized to give $$\label{str-pde-oscillation-gradient} \sup_{B_{1/2}}\|df\|_g\leq C\operatorname{osc}_{B_1} f,$$ provided the same fixed extension and the same structural constants apply on the patch. Smooth boundary data on finite boundary patches are allowed.
  - Explanation: Regularizes the flux and proves structural and gradient Hölder estimates uniform in the regularization after a bounded gradient range has been established.
- **claim-stress-global-gradient** (bound, [source](#stmt-str-pde-global-gradient)): Let $f$ be a classical regularized solution on a truncation $X_R$, with boundary values $D'$ at the finite boundary and zero at $r=R$, where $0\leq D'\leq D$. Then $$\label{str-pde-global-bounds} 0\leq f\leq D,\qquad \|df\|_g\leq M_D, \qquad f\leq C_Dr^{-\xi}\quad(r\geq r_1),$$ for any fixed $0<\xi<1$ and suitable $r_1,C_D,M_D$ independent of small $h$ and sufficiently large $R$.
  - Explanation: Bounds height, physical gradient, and end decay independently of the small regularization and distant outer truncation.
- **claim-stress-linear-end-bounds** (bound, [source](#stmt-str-pde-linear-end-bounds)): For the solution in Theorem <a href="#str-pde-fixed-height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="str-pde-fixed-height">13</a> there are $c,C,Q>0$ and a collar $0<z<z_0$ such that $$\label{str-pde-linear-bounds} cz\leq f\leq Cz,\qquad \|df\|_g\leq Qz.$$ These constants can be chosen uniformly for a family whenever the coarse bounds $f\leq C_0z^\xi$, a positive lower bound on one fixed inner sphere, local physical gradient bounds, and the compact metric bounds used in the proof are uniform.
  - Explanation: Proves linear height and physical-gradient decay at conformal infinity and identifies the data needed for family uniformity.
- **claim-stress-boundary-jet** (theorem, [source](#stmt-str-pde-boundary-jet)): Under <a href="#str-pde-prepared-end" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="str-pde-prepared-end">[str-pde-prepared-end]</a> and <a href="#str-pde-linear-bounds" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="str-pde-linear-bounds">[str-pde-linear-bounds]</a>, the expansion <a href="#str-pde-end-expansion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="str-pde-end-expansion">[str-pde-end-expansion]</a> holds.
  - Explanation: Derives the conformal boundary expansion from the prepared end and linear bounds.
- **claim-local-height-gradient** (bound, [source](#stmt-str-pde-local-gradient)): On a physical coordinate ball with uniformly bounded geometry, a solution with $0\leq f\leq H$ has a gradient bound on a concentric smaller ball depending only on $H$ and that geometry. The estimate applies uniformly to smooth solutions off their critical sets and to their $C^1$ limits.
  - Explanation: Controls the gradient on a smaller physical ball using local height and geometry, including the indicated limits.
- **claim-growing-heights-common-end** (theorem, [source](#stmt-str-pde-growing-heights)): Let $g_i$ be smooth metrics on the same exterior, with $H_{\partial X}(g_i)\leq0$, converging smoothly on compact subsets to a smooth metric $g$. Suppose that each has the prepared end required for Theorem <a href="#str-pde-fixed-height" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="str-pde-fixed-height">13</a>, and that for a common $\beta>1$ and $M<\infty$, $$\label{str-pde-uniform-physical-metrics} \sum_{j=0}^2\|\nabla_b^j(g_i-b)\|_b\leq Mz^\beta$$ on a common end. Assume the compact metrics are uniformly positive definite. Let $D_i\geq1$ be arbitrary finite heights and let $f_i$ be their solutions. Then on a common end collar there are constants $c,C,Q>0$, independent of $i,D_i$, such that $$\label{str-pde-uniform-linear-bounds} cz\leq f_i\leq Cz,\qquad \|df_i\|_{g_i}\leq Qz.$$ For some $\gamma>0$ the functions have uniform compact $C^{2,\gamma}$ bounds on a common smaller collar, which is noncritical for every $f_i$. After extraction, they converge in $C^{2,\gamma'}$ for $0<\gamma'<\gamma$ on a still smaller closed compact collar, and smoothly on interior compact subsets of that collar, to a solution for $g$. If $g$ has a smooth compactification in another defining function $\rho$ comparable to $z$, the limiting solution is smooth there and has $f=\rho C_\infty+O(\rho^2)$ with positive smooth $C_\infty$.
  - Explanation: Provides a common noncritical end collar and compact regularity despite arbitrary finite boundary heights; smoothness at the limiting boundary uses a smooth limiting compactification.
- **claim-full-cut-flux-saturation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-str-flux-saturation)): Let $f_D$ be the solution in Theorem <a href="#thm:str-stress-dirichlet" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:str-stress-dirichlet">[thm:str-stress-dirichlet]</a> on an exterior $(X,g)$ with inner boundary $T$, with $f_D\|_T=D>0$ and $f_D\to0$ at infinity. Write $f_D=zC_D(\omega)+O(z^2)$, and set $$\mathcal F_D=\int_{\mathbb S^2} C_D^2\,d\omega.$$ Then $$\int_X t(\|df_D\|)\|df_D\|\,dV_g=D\mathcal F_D, \qquad 0\leq\mathcal F_D\leq A_g(T), \qquad \lim_{D\to\infty}\mathcal F_D=A_g(T). \label{eq:str-flux-saturation}$$ In particular $$\fint_{\mathbb S^2}C_D^3\,d\omega \geq\left(\frac{\mathcal F_D}{4\pi}\right)^{3/2}. \label{eq:str-jensen}$$
  - Explanation: Shows that the conserved inward flux approaches the full cut infimum as boundary height grows, and bounds the cubic angular average.
- **claim-conserved-stress-smoothing** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-str-stress-identities)): For a solution $f$ of the saturating equation, put $\sigma=\|df\|$, $e=\nabla f/\|df\|$ at noncritical points, and $k=(1-t(\sigma)^{3/2})^{1/2}$. Define $$\mathcal P_{ee}=2k,\qquad \mathcal P\|_{e^\perp}=\frac{3+k^2}{2k}I,\qquad \mathcal P_{e\perp}=0, \qquad L=\mathcal P-\tfrac12(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_g\mathcal P)g. \label{eq:str-stress-definition}$$ At a critical point set $\mathcal P=2g$ and $L=-g$. These fields are continuous, smooth away from the critical set, and satisfy $$\operatorname{div}_g\mathcal P=0, \qquad (\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gL)^2-\|L\|_g^2=6, \qquad L<0. \label{eq:str-stress-identities}$$ If $K-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g\geq0$, then $\mathcal P:K\leq0$. Therefore $(g,K+L)$ satisfies the flat-cosmological DEC whenever $(g,K)$ satisfies the $\Lambda=-3$ DEC, with at least the original strict margin, and its future boundary expansion is strictly smaller.* *On any compact set where the DEC and expansion have strict margins, $\mathcal P$ can be smoothed preserving those margins. This is valid also at an original boundary face, using only the exterior side.
  - Explanation: Constructs the conserved stress and negative trace reversal, transfers the dominant energy condition to the flat normalization, and smooths while preserving strict compact margins.
- **claim-spherical-constraint-identities** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-str-bend-constraints)): Let $$q=F^{-1}ds^2+s^2\gamma,\qquad F>0,\qquad n=\sqrt F\,\partial_s.$$ Write the orthonormal blocks of a symmetric tensor $B$ as $$B_{nn}=-h,\qquad B_{nT}=G,\qquad B_T=-kI+U, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\gamma U=0.$$ Here $G$ and $U$ are represented by a one-form and a symmetric tracefree two-tensor on the unit sphere. Put $\mathcal H=R_q+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_qB)^2-\|B\|_q^2$ and $\mathcal D=\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_q(B-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_qB)q)$. Then $$R_q=\frac{2(1-F)}{s^2}-\frac{2\partial_sF}{s} -\frac{2\sqrt F}{s^2}\Delta_\gamma F^{-1/2}. \label{str-bc-scalar}$$ In particular, if $F=1+s^2k^2-2m/s$, then $$\mathcal H=\frac{4\partial_sm}{s^2} -\frac{2\sqrt F}{s^2}\Delta_\gamma F^{-1/2} +4k(h-k-s\partial_sk)-2\|G\|^2-\|U\|^2. \label{str-bc-hamiltonian}$$ For arbitrary $F$ the momentum components are $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal D_n&=\frac{2\sqrt F}{s}(k+s\partial_sk-h) +\frac{\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_\gamma G-2G\cdot\nabla_\gamma\log\sqrt F}{s}, \label{str-bc-momentum-normal}\\ \mathcal D_T&=\sqrt F(\partial_sG+3G/s) +\frac{1}{s}\bigl\{\nabla_\gamma(h+k) -(h-k)\nabla_\gamma\log\sqrt F\bigr\}\nonumber\\ &\hspace{12mm}+\frac{1}{s}\bigl\{\mathop{\mathrm{div}}_\gamma U -U\nabla_\gamma\log\sqrt F\bigr\}. \label{str-bc-momentum-tangent} \end{aligned}$$
  - Explanation: Gives exact scalar, Hamiltonian, and momentum formulas in the spherical block decomposition.
- **claim-small-cost-flat-bending** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-str-af-bending)): Suppose $(\Omega,g,B)$ is smooth, has one end, has strictly negative future boundary expansion, and satisfies $\mathcal H_g-2\|\mathcal D_g\|_g>0$ everywhere. Suppose its end is $g=e^{4v}b$, where $$v=r^{-3}v_3(\omega)-d_0r^{-3-\delta}+O_3(r^{-4}), \qquad 0<\delta<1,\quad d_0>0, \label{str-bc-prepared-v}$$ with smooth angular coefficients. Suppose also that on this end there are a positive smooth $C(\omega)$ and a unit covector $e$ such that $$B=-g+\frac{C^3}{r^3} \left(\frac12g-\frac32e\otimes e\right)+O_1(r^{-4}), \qquad e\otimes e=n_r^\flat\otimes n_r^\flat+O_1(r^{-1}), \label{str-bc-prepared-B}$$ where $n_r$ is the outward unit normal to the coordinate spheres. The scalar remainder has three symbol derivatives so that the change to the area coordinate has two controlled metric derivatives. The initial interpolation needs two derivatives of the metric error and one of the tensor error; the preparation in Lemma <a href="#lem:str-preparation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:str-preparation">11</a> supplies the stronger scalar expansion with all symbol derivatives.* *For every $\varepsilon>0$ and every fixed compact subset there exist smooth data $(q_\varepsilon,B_\varepsilon)$ agreeing with $(g,B)$ on that subset and near the original boundary, such that $$\begin{aligned} &q_\varepsilon\geq(1-\varepsilon)g, \label{str-bc-lower-comparison}\\ &R_{q_\varepsilon}+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}B_\varepsilon)^2-\|B_\varepsilon\|^2 -2\|\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(B_\varepsilon-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}B_\varepsilon)q_\varepsilon)\| \geq c_\varepsilon(1+s)^{-3-\delta}>0, \label{str-bc-strict-dec}\\ &q_\varepsilon-\delta_{\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_\infty(s^{-1}),\qquad R_{q_\varepsilon}=O_\infty(s^{-3-\delta}),\nonumber\\ &B_\varepsilon=O_\infty(s^{-2}),\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{q_\varepsilon}B_\varepsilon=0 \quad\hbox{on the final end}. \label{str-bc-af-bounds} \end{aligned}$$ Its metric ADM energy satisfies $$\fint_{\mathbb S^2}(8v_3-C^3/2) \leq E(q_\varepsilon) \leq\fint_{\mathbb S^2}(8v_3-C^3/2)+\varepsilon. \label{str-bc-energy}$$ Consequently its full-cut area infimum is at least $(1-\varepsilon)A_g(S)$.
  - Explanation: Bends a prepared hyperbolic end into a flat end with strict constraints, exact tail tracefreeness, controlled metric energy, and a lower cut-area comparison.
- **claim-flat-deformation-estimate** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-fl-deformation)): Let $(\Omega_{\mathrm{orig}},q,B)$ be smooth three-dimensional initial data on a connected orientable manifold with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S_0$. Assume that the metric space including $S_0$ is complete and has exactly one asymptotically Euclidean end. On that end, in Euclidean coordinates of radius $r$, suppose that, for some $0<\delta<1$, $$\label{eq:fl-data-decay} q-\delta_{\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_\infty(r^{-1}),\qquad R_q=O_\infty(r^{-3-\delta}),\qquad B=O_\infty(r^{-2}),\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_qB=0.$$ Here $O_\infty(r^{-a})$ includes all differentiated symbol estimates: each Euclidean derivative lowers the indicated order by one. Extend $r$ to a positive smooth function on the whole manifold. Suppose that there is $c_*>0$ such that $$\label{eq:fl-strict-dec} R_q+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_q B)^2-\lvert B\rvert_q^2 -2\bigl\lvert\operatorname{div}_q \bigl(B-(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_qB)q\bigr)\bigr\rvert_q \ge c_*(1+r)^{-3-\delta},$$ and that $H_q+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_{S_0}B<0$ on every component of $S_0$, with the normal pointing into the exterior.* *For every connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary $D\subset\Omega_{\mathrm{orig}}$, closed as a subset and with $\operatorname{int}D\subset\operatorname{int}\Omega_{\mathrm{orig}}$, that contains the entire sufficiently distant end and whose *full compact intrinsic boundary* is smoothly embedded and two-sided, use that entire boundary as an enclosing cut. Allow coincidence with components of $S_0$, and allow $D=\Omega_{\mathrm{orig}}$, whose cut is $S_0$. Set $$A_*=\inf_D\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_q(\partial D).$$ Then the metric ADM energy satisfies $$E_q\ge \sqrt{\frac{A_*}{16\pi}}.$$ The boundary, the intermediate cuts, and the compact interior topology are otherwise unrestricted.
  - Explanation: Bounds metric ADM energy by the full enclosing-area infimum under the stated flat decay, strict energy margin, and strictly negative future boundary expansion.
- **claim-total-bounding-trapped-region** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-mots-barriers)): Let $(M,g,Q)$ be a smooth compact three-manifold with boundary $\Gamma_-\sqcup\Gamma_+$. Every connected component of $M$ is required to meet $\Gamma_+$. The outer part $\Gamma_+$ has $\Theta_Q>0$ with its normal out of $M$. The required inner part $\Gamma_-$ may be empty; when present it has $\Theta_Q<0$ with its normal into $M$.* *Consider all smooth bounding domains that contain a relative collar of $\Gamma_-$, avoid $\Gamma_+$, and whose free boundary has $\Theta_Q\le0$ with the normal out of the domain. If this collection is nonempty, the closure of its union has smooth compact embedded stable MOTS free frontier. It is itself the closure of a bounding domain and contains every domain in the collection. If $\Gamma_-\ne\varnothing$, the strict inner and outer barriers give a nonempty smooth enclosing MOTS. Boundary parts and frontiers may be disconnected. No constraint or energy condition on $Q$ is required.
  - Explanation: Obtains the full smooth stable bounding MOTS frontier from the specified barriers and bounding-domain collection, without an energy condition on the tensor.
- **claim-right-continuous-thresholds** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-right-continuity)): Let $E_c$ be an increasing family of closed subsets of a fixed compact metric space. Except at a countable set of parameters, $$E_{c_j}\longrightarrow E_c \quad\hbox{in Hausdorff distance whenever }c_j\downarrow c.$$ At an empty $E_c$, this means that $E_{c'}$ is empty for all sufficiently close $c'>c$.
  - Explanation: Proves Hausdorff right continuity outside a countable exceptional set, including the stronger local persistence of emptiness.
- **claim-frontier-outward-collars** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-frontier-collars)): If $\Sigma$ is a connected component of the smooth frontier of a full maximal region at threshold $c$ for $Q$, it has a smooth outward foliation $\Sigma_s$, $0\le s<s_0$, such that $$\Theta_Q(\Sigma_0)=c,\qquad \Theta_Q(\Sigma_s)>c\quad(0<s<s_0).$$ The leaf parameter is a smooth defining function, and $\lvert\,\mathrm ds\rvert$ is bounded above and away from zero.
  - Explanation: Uses stability and maximality to produce an ordered smooth outward collar with expansion strictly above its frontier threshold.
- **claim-support-distance-error** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-support-parallel)): Suppose that the frontier of a closed set $E$ lies in a fixed compact interior region of smooth data $(M,g,Q)$, and has exterior-support expansion at most $c$. For sufficiently small $z>0$, the distance neighborhood $E_z=\{\operatorname{dist}(\,\cdot\,,E)\le z\}$ has exterior-support expansion at most $c+Cz$. The constant and the allowable radius depend only on the compact ambient geometry and $Q$, independently of the support’s curvature and the regularity of $E$.
  - Explanation: Controls the expansion of distance neighborhoods by an additive ambient error without a support-curvature bound.
- **claim-smooth-support-enclosure** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-support-enclosure)): Let $M$ be a smooth compact connected three-manifold with boundary $\Gamma_-\sqcup\Gamma_+$, where $\Gamma_+\ne\varnothing$. Let $E\ne\varnothing$ be closed, contain a relative collar of the required $\Gamma_-$ if it is present, and have positive distance from $\Gamma_+$. Suppose every exterior support of its interior frontier has $Q$-expansion at most $c$. If $$c'>c,\qquad \Theta_Q(\Gamma_+)>c'$$ with the outward normal of $M$, then $E$ is strictly enclosed by a smooth bounding domain whose free frontier has expansion $c'$. In particular it lies in the full closed trapped region at threshold $c'$. The enclosing domain and frontier may be disconnected.
  - Explanation: Strictly encloses a closed weak support barrier by a smooth bounding domain at a larger admissible expansion threshold.
- **claim-threshold-offset-preparation** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-threshold-preparation)): The thresholds and the prepared exterior above can be chosen so that both full threshold families are right-continuous at their chosen thresholds, the retained faces have disjoint collars as in Lemma <a href="#lem:fl-frontier-collars" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:fl-frontier-collars">28</a>, and Equation <a href="#eq:fl-cut-inclusion" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fl-cut-inclusion">[eq:fl-cut-inclusion]</a> holds. There are a smooth compactly supported $C$, constants $C_b>0>C_w$, positive collar constants $k_B$, and a smooth $\rho>0$, equal far out to a positive constant times $r^{-3-\delta}$, such that $$\begin{aligned} \label{eq:fl-offset-shape} &C_w\le C\le C_b,\qquad C=C_b-k_Bs\ \hbox{near }B_b,\qquad C=C_w+k_Bs\ \hbox{near }B_w,\\ \label{eq:fl-face-heights} &b_-=c_b-C_b<0,\qquad b_+=-c_w-C_w>0,\\ \label{eq:fl-margin} &\lvert(h+C)\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K\rvert+\lvert\,\mathrm dC\rvert+\rho \le M_d\qquad\hbox{for all }b_-\le h\le b_+ . \end{aligned}$$ All these data are fixed before the deformation parameters.
  - Explanation: Chooses compatible right-continuous thresholds, disjoint collars, offsets, and positive weights before deformation parameters are introduced.
- **claim-flat-flux-differentiation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-alg-flux)): For $U=l\sqrt D$, one has $$\begin{aligned} \tfrac12\nabla\log D &=H^f(w,\cdot)+pv\,\,\mathrm dt, \label{eq:fl-alg-D-derivative}\\ \nabla_iw_j &=(H^f A_d)_{ij}+pd\,(\,\mathrm dt)_i w_j, \label{eq:fl-alg-w-derivative}\\ \nabla\log u &=H^f(w,\cdot)+(2+p+pv)\,\mathrm dt. \label{eq:fl-alg-u-derivative} \end{aligned}$$ Set $$k=-H^f-p(\,\mathrm dt\otimes w^\flat+w^\flat\otimes\,\mathrm dt), \qquad Q=K-k.$$ Then the flux $V=uA_\chi(4\nabla Z+K(w,\cdot))$ satisfies $$\begin{aligned} \frac{V}{u} &=p_Q(w,\cdot)+4A_d\nabla t+wF, \label{eq:fl-alg-flux-identity}\\ \frac{\operatorname{div}(uw)}u &=F+(1-\chi)q_1-\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K+2(p+1)ax. \label{eq:fl-alg-uw-divergence} \end{aligned}$$ Every expression asserted to be an identity extends smoothly across $\,\mathrm df=0$.
  - Explanation: Derives differentiation, weighted divergence, and trace-adjusted flux identities with smooth continuation through critical points.
- **claim-flat-scalar-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-fl-alg-scalar)): Let $$\bar g=g+l^2\,\mathrm df^2,\qquad \hat g=e^{4t}\bar g.$$ For $\mathcal T$ in <a href="#eq:fl-quadratic-form" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fl-quadratic-form">[eq:fl-quadratic-form]</a>, the exact identity is $$\frac12 e^{4t}R_{\hat g} =8\pi\bigl(\mu+J(w)\bigr)+\mathcal T+w(F) -F\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K-\frac{\operatorname{div}V}{u}. \label{eq:fl-alg-identity}$$
  - Explanation: Expresses deformed scalar curvature using the constraints, actual trace, coercive quadratic form, and weighted flux divergence.
- **claim-flat-square-coercivity** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-alg-coercivity)): The expression <a href="#eq:fl-alg-invariant-quadratic" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fl-alg-invariant-quadratic">[eq:fl-alg-invariant-quadratic]</a> equals $\mathcal T$ in <a href="#eq:fl-quadratic-form" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fl-quadratic-form">[eq:fl-quadratic-form]</a>. It is smooth in the actual variables at $\,\mathrm df=0$. For an absolute constant $C$, if $0\le p\le N$, then $$F^2+\|P\|^2+\|M\|^2+dq_1^2+\|\,\mathrm dt\|_{A_d}^2 \le C(N+4)^2\mathcal T. \label{eq:fl-alg-general-coercivity}$$ At a point with $\,\mathrm dt=0$, put $\mathcal E=\|P^{\mathrm{tf}}\|^2+\|M\|^2+F^2+\chi q_1^2$. There is the stronger bound $$\frac12\mathcal E\le\mathcal T\le\mathcal E. \label{eq:fl-alg-floor-comparison}$$ These constants are independent of $d$, $p$, $N$, $l$, and the size of $\,\mathrm df$.
  - Explanation: Identifies the invariant quadratic expression with its square decomposition, proves smoothness at zero gradient, and separates general polynomial coercivity from the stronger floor comparison.
- **claim-floor-gauss-inequality** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-alg-floor-gauss)): For a symmetric tensor $A$, define $$\mathcal S(A) =\frac14(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A)^2-\frac12\|A_\perp^{\mathrm{tf}}\|^2 +dA_{ee}\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_\perp A-d\|A_{e\perp}\|^2.$$ At an interior floor contact, $$\frac12e^{4t}R_{\hat g} \le \frac12R_g-v\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e,e)+\mathcal S(H^f). \label{eq:fl-alg-floor-gauss}$$ The expression $v\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e,e)$ is interpreted as $\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g(w,w)$; all quantities have continuous, direction-independent values at $w=0$.
  - Explanation: Bounds the conformal scalar curvature at an interior minimum of the conformal variable; no vanishing graph gradient is assumed.
- **claim-uniform-floor-coercivity** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-alg-floor-coercivity)): At a point with $\,\mathrm dt=0$, for an absolute constant $C$, $$\mathcal T-\mathcal S(H^f) \ge \frac1{16}\mathcal T -C(1+N)^2\bigl(\|K\|^2+vF^2\bigr). \label{eq:fl-alg-floor-coercivity}$$ In particular the coefficient $1/16$ is independent of $N$ and of the graph gradient.
  - Explanation: Retains a uniform positive fraction of the quadratic form after subtracting the graph Gauss contribution, with explicit polynomial coefficient errors.
- **claim-floor-trace-drift-estimates** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-alg-floor-derivatives)): Assume the preceding hypotheses, $h=\tau f$, and $\|h\|\le C_0$. At any point where $\,\mathrm dt=0$, for each fixed $\eta>0$ there are constants $C_\eta$ and an integer $m$, independent of $N$, the homotopy parameters, and the graph gradient, such that $$\begin{aligned} w(F)&\ge \tau a\|\,\mathrm df\|-\eta\mathcal T -C_\eta(1+N)^m(\rho_0+v\rho_1), \label{eq:fl-alg-trace-derivative}\\ \left\|\frac{\operatorname{div}(uA_\chi K(w,\cdot))}{u}\right\| &\le\eta\mathcal T+C_\eta(\rho_0+v\rho_1). \label{eq:fl-alg-drift-derivative} \end{aligned}$$ If in addition $\|h\|\le Cr^{-\gamma}$ on the end, then $$\|K\|^2+vF^2\le C(\rho_0+v\rho_1). \label{eq:fl-alg-weighted-remainder}$$ The constants may depend on the fixed data, weights, compact corrections, height bound, and $\eta$; they are uniform over the three stages in <a href="#eq:fl-alg-stage-right-sides" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fl-alg-stage-right-sides">[eq:fl-alg-stage-right-sides]</a>.
  - Explanation: Controls the trace derivative and tensor-drift divergence at floor-stationary points, retaining the positive height derivative and weighted remainders.
- **claim-face-flux-mean-curvature** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-boundary-identity)): On any face where $f$ is constant, for the actual trace $F$, $$\label{eq:fl-boundary-identity} \frac{V_\nu}{u} =d(H+4\partial_\nu t)-H+w_\nu(F-P_B),\qquad H_{\hat g}=e^{-2t}\sqrt d\,(H+4\partial_\nu t).$$ In particular the physical boundary condition gives $H_{\hat g}=-e^{-2t}\sqrt d\,N_B<0$.
  - Explanation: Relates face flux to conformal mean curvature and shows that the physical inner condition enforces strict mean negativity.
- **claim-flat-continuation-family** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-fl-homotopies)): There is a continuous piecewise smooth family, with parameter $\xi\in[0,4]$, starting at Equations <a href="#eq:fl-trace" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fl-trace">[eq:fl-trace]</a>, <a href="#eq:fl-scalar" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fl-scalar">[eq:fl-scalar]</a>, and <a href="#eq:fl-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:fl-boundary">[eq:fl-boundary]</a>, and ending at the zero trace solution and scalar equation with zero source and inner flux. In the first three stages the source is the $\Xi$ just defined, always evaluated using the current trace $F$. Every trace right side has derivative at least one in $h$, at fixed point, $Z$, and $\,\mathrm df$. The outer values remain $f=Z=0$.
  - Explanation: Connects the physical system to a zero endpoint while preserving strict height monotonicity and outer Dirichlet values.
- **claim-flat-height-outer-control** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-height)): Every smooth trace solution in Proposition <a href="#prop:fl-homotopies" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:fl-homotopies">41</a> satisfies $\lvert h\rvert\le C_0$, and its actual trace satisfies $\lvert F\rvert\le C_F$, independently of $N,R,\xi$ and the input $Z$. There are fixed $r_0,C>0$ and a lower bound $R_{\mathrm{ht}}(N)$ such that, when $R\ge R_{\mathrm{ht}}(N)$, $$\label{eq:fl-end-height} \lvert h\rvert\le C(r^{-\gamma}-R^{-\gamma}) \quad(r_0\le r\le R),\qquad \lvert\,\mathrm df\rvert\le C\tau^{-1}R^{-1-\gamma}\quad\hbox{on }S_R .$$ The constants in the bound are independent of $N,R,\xi$. For fixed $N,\epsilon$, increasing the lower bound on $R$ ensures $t>-\epsilon$ at the outer boundary of every such solution.
  - Explanation: Bounds trace height and end barriers independently of the large parameter and homotopy, with an outer radius chosen afterward to exclude boundary floor contact.
- **claim-floor-divergence-ledger** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fl-floor-ledger)): There exist $c_0>0$ and polynomial constants $C_N$ such that every smooth first-three-stage solution with $t\ge-\epsilon$, at an interior point with $t=-\epsilon$, satisfies $$\label{eq:fl-floor-divergence} u^{-1}\operatorname{div}V_\lambda \ge c_0\mathcal T+\tau a\sigma-C_N(\rho_0+v\rho_1).$$ Here $c_0$ can be chosen independently of $N,R,\xi$.
  - Explanation: Derives a coercive lower bound with a polynomial adverse remainder at a proposed interior floor contact; strict exclusion follows only after the penalty is chosen.
- **claim-flat-floor-separation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-fl-floor)): Fix $0<\delta_0<\min\{c_0/2,1/4\}$, where $c_0$ is from Lemma <a href="#lem:fl-floor-ledger" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:fl-floor-ledger">43</a>. There is a polynomial choice of $\Pi_N$ such that, for all sufficiently large $N$, followed by all $R\ge R_{\mathrm{floor}}(N,\epsilon)$, no smooth solution of Proposition <a href="#prop:fl-homotopies" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:fl-homotopies">41</a> satisfies $t\ge-\epsilon$ and attains $t=-\epsilon$. Every such solution has $t>-\epsilon$ on the closed truncation.
  - Explanation: Chooses a polynomial penalty to rule out interior and boundary floor contacts throughout the continuation.
- **claim-rank-one-gradient-hessian** (bound, [source](#stmt-reg-rank-one)): Let $U$ be an interior coordinate ball or a smooth boundary half-ball, with a uniformly controlled $C^2$ metric $g$. In the boundary case use Gaussian coordinates, so $g_{33}=1$ and $g_{a3}=0$ for $a=1,2$. Suppose that $z$ is smooth on $U$, up to the face on its original side in the boundary case, and satisfies $$A^{ij}\nabla_i\nabla_j z=G,\qquad A^{ij}=g^{ij}-(1-b)e^i e^j,\qquad e=\frac{\nabla z}{\|\nabla z\|},\qquad c_0\le b\le1, \label{reg-trace-equation}$$ where $c_0>0$. In the boundary case assume that $z$ is constant on the face. At a zero of $\nabla z$, an arbitrary measurable unit direction is allowed, provided Equation <a href="#reg-trace-equation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="reg-trace-equation">[reg-trace-equation]</a> holds with that choice. Assume $\|\nabla z\|\le L$ and $\|G\|\le Q$. There are $\alpha\in(0,1)$, a uniform positive radius $r_0$, and $C$, depending only on $c_0$, the indicated geometry, and separation from the other faces of the patch, such that on a smaller patch $$\\|Dz\\|_{C^{0,\alpha}}\le C(L+Q),\qquad \int_{B_r(x)\cap U}\|\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}z\|^2\,dV_g \le C(L+Q)^2r^{1+2\alpha}\quad(0<r\le r_0). \label{reg-main-estimates}$$ The constants $\alpha,r_0,C$ do not depend on a modulus of continuity of $b$ or $G$. The same assertion holds for uniformly controlled families of patches.
  - Explanation: Proves local gradient Hölder and Hessian energy estimates for a gradient-aligned uniformly elliptic rank-one matrix, including reflected boundary patches, without coefficient continuity moduli.
- **claim-cutoff-integrability-exponent** (bound, [source](#stmt-reg-cutoff)): There is $p_0\in(2,3)$ depending only on $c_0$ with the following property. If $g$ is sufficiently close to the Euclidean metric in $L^\infty$, with bounded first derivatives, then the operator in Equation <a href="#reg-trace-equation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="reg-trace-equation">[reg-trace-equation]</a>, with its coefficients held fixed, satisfies the interior estimate $$\\|v\\|_{W^{2,p_0}(B_{1/2})} \le C\bigl(\\|v\\|_{L^{p_0}(B_1)} +\\|A^{ij}\nabla_i\nabla_jv\\|_{L^{p_0}(B_1)}\bigr). \label{reg-cutoff-estimate}$$ It also satisfies the analogous estimate with exponent two. The coefficient direction in this assertion need not be the gradient direction of $v$.
  - Explanation: Obtains Hessian estimates at an exponent above two and below the spatial dimension by absorption near the Laplacian, without derivatives of the measurable axis or coefficient.
- **claim-fixed-axis-regularity** (bound, [source](#stmt-reg-fixed-axis)): Let $a$ be a fixed Euclidean unit vector and let $c_0\le b(x)\le1$ be measurable. If $Y\in W^{2,2}(B_{3/4})$ satisfies $$\Delta_{a^\perp}Y+bY_{aa}=0, \label{reg-fixed-equation}$$ then for some $\alpha_1\in(0,1)$ depending only on $c_0$, $$\\|Y\\|_{C^{1,\alpha_1}(B_{1/4})} \le C\\|Y\\|_{W^{2,2}(B_{3/4})}. \label{reg-fixed-axis-estimate}$$
  - Explanation: Converts the fixed-axis equation into a scalar divergence equation for an axial derivative and controls the remaining gradient by a Newton potential.
- **claim-drop-affine-dichotomy** (theorem, [source](#stmt-reg-dichotomy)): Fix $r_*\in(0,1/32]$. For every $h_*>0$ there are $k_*\in(r_*,1)$ and $\varepsilon_*>0$ with the following property. For a normalized solution on $B_1$ in the class of Equation <a href="#reg-supersolution" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="reg-supersolution">[reg-supersolution]</a>, with errors at most $\varepsilon_*$, either $$\sup_{B_{r_*}}\|\nabla z\|\le k_* , \label{reg-drop}$$ or there is an affine $L$ such that $$\sup_{B_{r_*}}\|z-L\|\le h_*r_* , \qquad \tfrac12\le \|DL\|\le2. \label{reg-affine-alternative}$$ If the center lies on the reflecting plane and $z$ has zero boundary value, $L$ can be chosen odd about that plane.
  - Explanation: Shows that normalized solutions either lose gradient amplitude or admit a nondegenerate affine approximation, with odd approximations at boundary centers.
- **claim-affine-improvement** (bound, [source](#stmt-reg-improvement)): There are $\alpha_2\in(0,\alpha_1)$, $r_2\in(0,1/8)$, and $\eta_0,h_0>0$ depending only on $c_0$ such that the following holds. Suppose $g(0)=I$, $\|\nabla z\|\le8$, $$\\|z-L_0\\|_{L^\infty(B_1)}\le h\le h_0, \qquad \tfrac14\le \|DL_0\|\le4, \qquad \\|G\\|_\infty+\\|g-I\\|_\infty+\\|Dg\\|_\infty\le h\eta_0.$$ Then an affine $L_1$ satisfies $$\\|z-L_1\\|_{L^\infty(B_{r_2})} \le h r_2^{1+\alpha_2},\qquad \|DL_1-DL_0\|\le Ch. \label{reg-improved-flatness}$$ If $z$ and $L_0$ are odd about a reflecting plane through the center, then $L_1$ can also be chosen odd.
  - Explanation: Improves an existing affine approximation on a smaller scale by comparison with a fixed-axis solution and a small correction.
- **claim-natural-growth-holder** (bound, [source](#stmt-reg-natural-growth)): Suppose $Z$ is locally Lipschitz, $\|Z\|\le M$, and satisfies, in distributions on a ball in $\mathbb R^3$, $$\mathop{\mathrm{div}}(aDZ+B)=e, \qquad \lambda I\le a=a^T\le\Lambda I, \qquad \\|B\\|_\infty\le B_0, \label{reg-natural-equation}$$ where $a$ is measurable and $e$ is a signed Radon measure. Assume $$\|e\|\le C_0(1+\|DZ\|^2)\,dx+\mu, \qquad \mu(B_r(x))\le C_\mu r^{1+\beta}, \qquad 0<\beta\le1, \label{reg-natural-measure}$$ for all smaller balls, where $\mu$ is nonnegative. Then $Z$ has a local $C^{0,\theta}$ bound for some $\theta>0$, depending only on the displayed constants and the patch separation. No bound for its local Lipschitz constant enters this estimate. The conclusion also holds at a smooth boundary with bounded total conormal flux, or with constant Dirichlet value.
  - Explanation: Obtains scalar Hölder control from bounded height, natural gradient growth, and a subcritical measure bound, including total-flux and constant-Dirichlet boundaries.
- **claim-coupled-classical-bootstrap** (theorem, [source](#stmt-reg-coupled-bootstrap)): Consider a family of smooth solutions $(f,Z)$ on smooth finite domains with uniformly controlled interior and boundary patches. Assume $\|f\|+\|Df\|+\|Z\|\le M$ and the following structural bounds, uniformly in the family:* 1. *The $f$-equation has the form of Equation <a href="#reg-trace-equation" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="reg-trace-equation">[reg-trace-equation]</a>, with $b\ge c_0>0$ and bounded $G$. Its actual matrix and source are smooth functions of $(x,Z,f,Df)$ on the bounded variable range, including at $Df=0$. The value of $f$ on each boundary face is constant.* 2. *After multiplication by the coordinate volume density, the $Z$-equation is $$\partial_i\bigl(a^{ij}(x,Z,f,Df)\partial_jZ +B^i(x,Z,f,Df)\bigr)=Q, \qquad \|Q\|\le C(1+\|DZ\|^2+\|D^2f\|^2), \label{reg-coupled-Z}$$ where $a$ is symmetric and uniformly elliptic and $B$ is bounded. The functions $a,B$ and $Q$, as a function also of $(DZ,D^2f)$, are smooth on the ranges on which they are used.* 3. *Each boundary component for $Z$ has either constant Dirichlet data, or bounded total conormal flux. In the latter case its equation can also be solved as $$\partial_\nu Z=H(x,Z,f,Df), \label{reg-normal-data}$$ where $H$ is smooth on the bounded variable range. These faces are disjoint and have no edges where the type of data changes.* *Assume that the derivatives of the displayed smooth functions and the geometry are bounded to the order needed for each stated estimate. Then $f$ and $Z$ have uniform local classical estimates of every such finite order, including at the boundary. The constants are independent of the size of a finite exhaustion domain if the patch geometry and all the displayed data bounds are independent of that size.
  - Explanation: Bootstraps bounded scalar variables to every finite classical order supported by the data, after checking the actual trace, source, ellipticity, and boundary interfaces.
- **claim-compact-height-separation** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fc-compact-separation)): In the first two stages, if a fixed compact subset $Q$ of the closed prepared exterior is disjoint from $\mathcal B_{c_b}$, there are $\eta_Q>0$ and $N_Q$ such that $$h\ge b_-+\eta_Q\quad\hbox{on }Q$$ for $N\ge N_Q$ and all sufficiently large allowed truncations. If $Q$ is disjoint from $\mathcal W_{c_w}$, then instead $h\le b_+-\eta_Q$. The compact sets may meet a face of the opposite color. These assertions are uniform over the two stage parameters.
  - Explanation: Uses relaxed height limits, all exterior supports, smooth enclosure, and threshold right continuity to separate compact sets from the opposite extreme height.
- **claim-signed-collar-slopes** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fc-collar-slopes)): For sufficiently large $N$, the first two stages satisfy, with fixed $c,C_1>0$, $$\label{eq:fc-signed-slopes} \frac c\tau\le\partial_\nu f\le\frac{C_1}\tau\quad\hbox{on }B_b, \qquad \frac c\tau\le-\partial_\nu f\le\frac{C_1}\tau\quad\hbox{on }B_w.$$ In the third stage $\|\partial_\nu f\|\le C_1/\tau$. In the first two stages $b_-\le h\le b_+$ on every fixed compact region needed for the scalar-curvature comparison.
  - Explanation: Proves signed collar slope bounds in the physical stages and absolute bounds in the later trace interpolation, then confines the physical compact height range.
- **claim-native-weight-trace** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fc-trace-estimate)): Let $\mathcal C$ be a fixed union of shortened inner collars. In the first two stages, for every nonnegative smooth $\phi$, $$\begin{aligned} \int_B L\phi\,dA_g &\le P_N\int_{\mathcal C}u \bigl((1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\phi+\|d\phi\|_{A_\chi}\bigr) \,dV_g,\label{eq:fc-weighted-trace}\\ \int_B \phi\,dA_g &\le P_N\int_{\mathcal C}\sqrt D \bigl((1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\phi+\|d\phi\|_{A_\chi}\bigr) \,dV_g.\label{eq:fc-unweighted-trace} \end{aligned}$$ Fixed collar cutoffs equal to one on $B$ are understood; their derivatives are included in the coefficient of $\phi$.
  - Explanation: Bounds weighted and unweighted face integrals by collar bulk terms with polynomial constants and no inverse collar scale.
- **claim-high-level-graph-energy** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fc-high-energy)): In stage one there is $M_0=M_0(N)>0$ such that, if $j_0$ is a smooth increasing cutoff equal to zero below $M_0$ and to one above $M_0+1$, with bounded derivative, then $$\label{eq:fc-high-energy} \int_{\Omega_R}u j_0 (\mathcal T+\rho+\tau a\sigma)\,dV_g +\int_{\Omega_R}u j_0'\|dZ\|_{A_\chi}^2\,dV_g \le C_N.$$ Consequently, on the ordinary product graph $\Gamma$ of $f$, every fixed compact base patch $Q$ satisfies $$\label{eq:fc-graph-L2} \int_{\Gamma\|Q}e^{2Z}\,dV_\Gamma\le C_{N,Q}.$$
  - Explanation: Establishes high-level weighted bulk energy and a local exponential graph-volume bound before any uniform upper bound on the scalar variable.
- **claim-graph-supremum-iteration** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fc-graph-iteration)): In stage one, $Z$ has a uniform upper bound on every fixed compact subset of the closed prepared exterior. The bound is independent of the truncation and first-stage parameter at fixed $N$.
  - Explanation: Combines graph Sobolev and exponential energy estimates with interpolation to bound the scalar variable on compact sets including inner faces.
- **claim-all-stage-bounded-variables** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-fc-bounded-range)): There are $N_0$ and $R_{\min}(N)\to\infty$ such that, for $N\ge N_0$ and $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$, every smooth solution of the four-stage family with $t\ge-\epsilon$ satisfies $$\|h\|\le C_0,\qquad \|f\|\le C_0/\tau, \qquad-\epsilon\le t\le Z\le C_N, \qquad \|df\|\le C_N.$$ The constants are uniform in the homotopy and truncation.
  - Explanation: Obtains bounded variables and graph gradients throughout the continuation, uniform in truncation at fixed deformation parameters.
- **claim-flat-classical-bounds** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-fc-classical-bounds)): At fixed $\epsilon,N$, the solutions in Proposition <a href="#prop:fc-bounded-range" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:fc-bounded-range">58</a> have local bounds of every finite classical order, up to the inner and outer faces, uniform in $\xi$ and in all sufficiently large $R$. On the end one can use patches with a fixed positive radius and uniform constants.
  - Explanation: Checks the rank-one and natural-growth interfaces and obtains finite classical estimates uniform in the homotopy and distant truncation.
- **claim-bounded-input-trace-solve** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-fc-trace-solve)): Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian three-manifold with smooth, disjoint boundary components carrying constant Dirichlet values. For prescribed $Z\in C^{1,b'}(M)$, $0<b'<1$, consider $$\label{eq:fc-general-trace} A_b(x,Z,Df):\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_g f=Q(x,Z,f,Df), \qquad A_b=I+(b-1)e\otimes e, \quad e=\nabla f/\|df\|.$$ Suppose the actual coefficients extend smoothly at $df=0$, are smooth on bounded ranges of their displayed variables, and the principal coefficient is independent of the height $f$. Suppose, uniformly on bounded input sets and any auxiliary compact parameter family, the following hold:* 1. *constant upper and lower height barriers bound $\|f\|\le M_1$ for every solution and for the normalized interpolation to $\Delta_g f=c_*f$, with fixed $c_*>0$;* 2. *on that height range, $0<b\le1$, $b\ge c/(1+\|df\|)$, and $\|Q\|\le C(1+\|df\|)$;* 3. *$Q_f>0$, uniformly away from zero on bounded variable ranges.* *Then the Dirichlet equation has a unique solution in $C^{3,b'}$. It depends continuously on the input and parameters and is bounded in $C^{3,b'}$ on bounded input sets. No prospective floor condition on an implicit auxiliary variable is required.
  - Explanation: Proves unique scalar Dirichlet solvability and bounded-input continuity using height barriers, a two-point gradient argument, and strict source monotonicity without a prospective floor.
- **claim-flat-trace-operator** (construction, [source](#stmt-cor-fc-flat-trace-solve)): For fixed $N\ge4$, $\tau>0$, a finite $\Omega_R$, and any $\xi\in[0,4]$, the trace equation of Proposition <a href="#prop:fl-homotopies" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:fl-homotopies">41</a> has a unique solution $f=S_\xi(Z)\in C^{3,b'}$ for every $Z\in C^{1,b'}$ with zero outer value. It has the continuity and bounded-input estimates of Proposition <a href="#prop:fc-trace-solve" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:fc-trace-solve">60</a>, without a floor assumption.
  - Explanation: Applies the general scalar solve to define the unique flat trace operator for every bounded smooth input, without imposing a floor.
- **claim-moving-section-degree** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-fc-moving-degree)): Let $X$ be a Banach space and $H:[0,1]\times X\to X$ a continuous map taking bounded sets to relatively compact sets. Let $\mathcal O\subset[0,1]\times X$ be a bounded relatively open set. If its closure has no fixed point on its relative product boundary, then $\deg(I-H_s,\mathcal O_s,0)$ is independent of $s$. Here $\mathcal O_s=\{x:(s,x)\in\mathcal O\}$, and the degree of an empty section is zero.
  - Explanation: Establishes degree invariance on moving open sections when the relative product boundary contains no fixed point.
- **claim-flat-finite-domain-existence** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-fc-degree)): For each fixed sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, all sufficiently large $N$, and every $R\ge R_{\min}(N)$, the physical flat system has a smooth solution on $\Omega_R$ with $t> -\epsilon$ on its closure. Its classical local bounds are uniform as $R\to\infty$ at fixed $N$.
  - Explanation: Defines a compact scalar map after the trace solve and uses the zero endpoint degree and floor exclusion to obtain a physical finite-domain solution.
- **claim-flat-exterior-existence** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-fc-existence)): For every fixed sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$ and sufficiently large $N$, the physical system has a smooth solution on $\Omega$, including its inner boundary, with $t\ge-\epsilon$. For some $c_N>0$ and every fixed derivative order $j$, $$\label{eq:fc-end-decay} \|\nabla^j f\|\le C_{N,j}e^{-c_Nr},\qquad Z,t=O_2(r^{-1}).$$ The differences $Z-t$ and $l^2df^2$, with their derivatives, decay exponentially. Moreover $$\label{eq:fc-flux-asymptotic} V=4\nabla_g t+O(r^{-3}),\qquad \mathcal F_N:=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}V_{\nu_g}\,dA_g \quad\hbox{exists and is finite}.$$
  - Explanation: Passes to the complete exterior by compact exhaustion and proves normalized end decay and existence of the limiting vector flux.
- **claim-flat-comparison-metric** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-fc-comparison-metric)): The solution of Proposition <a href="#prop:fc-existence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:fc-existence">64</a> defines $$\widehat g=e^{4t}(g+l^2df^2)$$ as a smooth complete metric on $\Omega$, with $R_{\widehat g}\ge0$ and strictly negative mean curvature on $B$ in the normal into $\Omega$. Its end satisfies $$\widehat g-\delta_{\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_2(r^{-1}),\qquad R_{\widehat g}=O(r^{-3-\delta}),\qquad E_{\widehat g}=E_g-\frac{\mathcal F_N}{8\pi}.$$
  - Explanation: Produces a complete scalar-nonnegative comparison metric with mean-negative inner boundary and computes its metric ADM energy change.
- **claim-flat-vanishing-flux-loss** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-fc-flux-loss)): For fixed $\epsilon>0$, $$\mathcal F_N\ge-\varepsilon_N, \qquad 0\le\varepsilon_N\le P_N(\ell+\ell^2/\tau)\longrightarrow0.$$ The constants in this estimate do not use the fixed-$N$ classical regularity constants.
  - Explanation: Bounds the negative flux defect by explicit small profile factors using polynomial estimates rather than fixed-parameter classical constants.
- **claim-flat-mass-completion** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-fc-mass-completion)): The flat exterior of Theorem <a href="#thm:fl-deformation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:fl-deformation">25</a> satisfies $$E_g\ge\sqrt{\frac{A_*}{16\pi}}.$$
  - Explanation: Applies the Riemannian Penrose theorem to the full outermost minimal comparison frontier and passes ordered numerical limits.
- **claim-general-time-component-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-ah-component)): Let $(\Omega,g,K)$ satisfy the regularity, completeness, one-end, dominant energy, weighted integrability, and future boundary hypotheses of the initial-data class, with $$g-b\in C^{2,\alpha}_{\tau_{\rm data}},\qquad K\in C^{1,\alpha}_{\tau_{\rm data}},\qquad \frac32<\tau_{\rm data}<3 .$$ Suppose the four metric fluxes in the designated chart are finite. There is no causal or sign assumption on their vector in this theorem. Then $$p_0(g)\ge \sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{16\pi}} \left(1+\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{4\pi}\right). \label{eq:ah-component-bound}$$ The tensor $K$ may have arbitrary trace, and the boundary may have arbitrarily many components.
  - Explanation: Bounds the metric time flux for general second fundamental form and arbitrary boundary components without assuming any causal character of the comparison covector.
- **claim-strict-hyperbolic-approximation** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-preparation)): There are smooth data $(g_j,K_j)$ converging to $(g,K)$ on compact sets, whose metric bilinear ratios converge uniformly to one, such that all four metric mass components converge and $$\label{eq:ah-prepared-data} \begin{split} &8\pi(\mu_j-\|J_j\|_{g_j})\ge c_j(1+r)^{-3-\delta}, \qquad H_{g_j}+\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_TK_j<0,\\ &g_j-b=O_\infty(r^{-\kappa}),\qquad K_j=O_\infty(r^{-\kappa}),\qquad R_{g_j}+6=O_\infty(r^{-3-\delta}) \end{split}$$ for positive constants $c_j$. In particular $A_{\min}(S;g_j)\to A_{\min}(S;g)$.
  - Explanation: Improves end decay and strict energy and boundary margins while preserving all metric flux limits and the full enclosing-area infimum.
- **claim-spatial-lapse-profile** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-lapse)): There is a positive smooth function $\lambda$, constant on a fixed large compact region containing all boundary collars, and equal to $\sqrt{A_0^2+r^2}$ far out, such that, with $s=d\log\lambda$, $$\label{eq:ah-lapse-inequalities} \|s\|\le1,\qquad E:=\frac{\Delta\lambda-\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\lambda(w,w)}{\lambda} +v\|s\|_{A_d}^2\le3 .$$ Here $w$ is any vector of length less than one, $v=\|w\|^2$, and $A_d=I-w\otimes w$. On the end, also $$E\le E_0:=\Delta\lambda/\lambda\le3,\qquad E_0=3+O(r^{-2}).$$ A fixed smooth positive $\rho$, radial of order $-3-\delta$ on the end, may be chosen with $10\rho<M_d$, and the lapse can be chosen so that $\|s\|\|K\|\le c_*\sqrt\rho$ for any prescribed sufficiently small $c_*>0$.
  - Explanation: Constructs a lapse constant on the boundary collars with controlled spatial curvature terms and sufficiently small coupling to the original tensor.
- **claim-hyperbolic-curvature-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-ah-alg-curvature)): With the preceding definitions, put $$V=uA_\chi\bigl(4\nabla Z+K(w,\cdot)^\sharp+A(w)w\bigr). \label{eq:ah-alg-V}$$ Then the following identity holds pointwise: $$\begin{aligned} \frac12e^{4t}(R_{\widehat g}+6) ={}&8\pi\bigl(\mu+J(w)\bigr)+3(e^{4t}-1) +4\langle A,\mathrm dt\rangle_{A_d} +\mathcal T \notag\\ &+w(F)-F\operatorname{tr}_gK-u^{-1}\operatorname{div}_g V . \label{eq:ah-alg-curvature-identity} \end{aligned}$$ Here $F$ denotes the actual trace $\operatorname{tr}_{A_\chi}S$; therefore the identity applies to any prescribed trace equation by substituting that prescription for $F$.
  - Explanation: Extends the graph curvature identity to a spatially varying lapse, retaining the actual trace and its derivative.
- **claim-spatial-primitive-cancellation** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-ah-alg-primitive)): Suppose the lapse is the profile defined in Section <a href="#subsec:ah-profiles" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="subsec:ah-profiles">7.2</a>; in particular $l_0(t,x)=e^{n(x)t}$ for $t\le0$ and $l_0(0,x)=1$. Define $$\begin{gathered} G(t,x)=\lambda(x)\int_{-\infty}^t L(z,x)\,\mathrm dz,\qquad G_c(x)=G(0,x)=\frac{\lambda(x)}{n(x)+2},\notag\\ V_*=V-4\sqrt D\,A_d\nabla_xG+4\nabla G_c . \label{eq:ah-alg-primitive-definitions} \end{gathered}$$ Assume the scalar equation of Equation <a href="#eq:ah-system" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-system">[eq:ah-system]</a> is written as $$u^{-1}\operatorname{div}_gV =3(e^{4t}-1)+4\langle A,\mathrm dt\rangle_{A_d}+\mathcal P,$$ where, for the physical system, $$\mathcal P=d_0(\mathcal T+\tau A_Ra\sigma) +\rho-m_0 n^{P_0}(\rho_0+v),\qquad \sigma=\|\mathrm df\|.$$ Put $$b_1=\frac{G}{\lambda L},\qquad s_G=\mathrm d_x\log G,\qquad X_1=x_t+\frac{a q_1}{4+pv}.$$ Then $$u^{-1}\operatorname{div}_gV_*=\mathcal P+\mathcal R, \label{eq:ah-alg-primitive-divergence}$$ where $$\begin{aligned} \mathcal R={}&3(e^{4t}-1)-4b_1E_G +\frac{4\sqrt d}{\lambda L}\Delta_gG_c\notag\\ &+4b_1\left\{ s_G(w)\bigl(F-\operatorname{tr}_{A_d}K+pdaX_1\bigr) -pv\langle(s_G)_{e^\perp},y\rangle \right\}, \label{eq:ah-alg-primitive-residual}\\ E_G={}&\frac{\Delta_xG-\nabla_x^2G(w,w)}{G} +v\langle s_G,A\rangle_{A_d}. \label{eq:ah-alg-EG} \end{aligned}$$ Here $\Delta_xG$ and $\nabla_x^2G$ differentiate $x\mapsto G(t,x)$ with $t$ fixed. If $\lambda$ and $n$ are spatially constant on a boundary collar, then $V_*=V$ on that collar.
  - Explanation: Defines a centered spatial primitive whose correction cancels the mixed lapse derivative and leaves the inner collar flux unchanged.
- **claim-hyperbolic-quadratic-coercivity** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-alg-coercivity)): For $p\ge0$ and $0<d\le1$, the form in Equation <a href="#eq:ah-alg-T" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-alg-T">[eq:ah-alg-T]</a> satisfies $$\mathcal T\ge\frac23F^2+[4(p+1)-v]\|y\|^2 +4(p+1)dX_1^2 . \label{eq:ah-alg-coercivity}$$
  - Explanation: Extracts uniform control of the trace and the shifted axial and transverse derivatives by exact square completion.
- **claim-four-flux-mass-passage** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-ah-alg-mass-passage)): Suppose $g$ has an asymptotically hyperbolic end with background $b$ and four finite metric fluxes $p_a(g)$, $a=0,1,2,3$, in the designated chart, as defined in Equation <a href="#eq:setup-flux" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:setup-flux">[eq:setup-flux]</a>. Assume that, outside a compact set, $n$ is a constant and $\lambda=\sqrt{A_0^2+r^2}$, with fixed $A_0>0$. Assume the differentiated end bounds $$\begin{gathered} g-b=O_2(r^{-\kappa}),\qquad K=O_1(r^{-\kappa}),\\ t=O_2(r^{-s}),\qquad w=O_2(r^{-\beta}),\\ \kappa>\frac32,\qquad s>\frac32,\qquad\beta>\frac32,\qquad \kappa+\beta>3 . \end{gathered} \label{eq:ah-alg-end-W}$$ Finally, suppose that for some $\delta>0$, $$R_{\widehat g}+6=O(r^{-3-\delta}). \label{eq:ah-alg-end-R}$$ Then all four metric fluxes of $\widehat g$ exist and are finite. For each $a=0,1,2,3$, $$p_a(\widehat g)-p_a(g) =-\frac1{2\pi} \lim_{r\to\infty} \int_{S_r}(V_a\,\mathrm dt-t\,\mathrm dV_a)(\nu_b) \,\mathrm dA_b . \label{eq:ah-alg-four-flux}$$ Moreover, $$V_*=4(\lambda\nabla_gt-t\nabla_g\lambda)+o(r^{-2}), \label{eq:ah-alg-Vstar-asymptote}$$ and the time-component identity is $$p_0(\widehat g)-p_0(g) =-\frac1{8\pi}\lim_{r\to\infty} \int_{S_r}g(V_*,\nu_g)\,\mathrm dA_g . \label{eq:ah-alg-time-flux}$$
  - Explanation: Proves existence of every deformed metric flux and identifies conformal mass changes and the centered time flux under differentiated decay and scalar-curvature integrability.
- **claim-end-scalar-integrability** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-alg-scalar-decay)): Suppose the differentiated bounds of Equation <a href="#eq:ah-alg-end-W" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-alg-end-W">[eq:ah-alg-end-W]</a> hold, $R_g+6=O(r^{-3-\delta})$, and $$2s>3+\delta,\qquad 2\beta>3+\delta.$$ Suppose also that the scalar end equation has the form $$\Delta_gZ+C(Z)\|\mathrm dZ\|_g^2 =\frac34(e^{4Z}-1)+O(r^{-3-\delta}), \label{eq:ah-alg-end-equation}$$ where $C$ is smooth and bounded near zero for the fixed profiles. Then Equation <a href="#eq:ah-alg-end-R" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-alg-end-R">[eq:ah-alg-end-R]</a> holds. In the deformation equations one takes $$C(Z)=p(Z)+2-d_0(Z)\bigl(p(Z)+1\bigr)$$ on the tail with spatially constant $n$.
  - Explanation: Uses the actual scalar end equation to obtain the curvature decay needed for mass convergence; near-critical conformal decay alone is insufficient.
- **claim-hyperbolic-height-offset-budget** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-heights)): For all sufficiently large $N$, and all sufficiently distant outer truncations at fixed profiles, every smooth solution in the first three stages satisfying $t\ge-\epsilon$ obeys $$\label{eq:ah-height-bounds} \|\tau f\|\le B,\qquad \|h\|\le Br^{-\beta}\quad(r\ge r_0).$$ The outer normal slope obeys the differentiated rate of the same radial barrier, and $t>-\epsilon$ on the outer face. The constants $B,r_0$ may be chosen independently of collar widths and collar derivatives, uniformly while the thresholds and correction amplitudes range in fixed bounded sets.* *The thresholds and offsets can consequently be fixed so that, on every physical solution obtained below, $$\label{eq:ah-offset-budget} \|F\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K\|+\|\nabla C\|\le2\rho .$$ The fixed region on which $n=N$ can be chosen to contain every compact sublevel set used in the boundary slope argument.
  - Explanation: Derives height and end barriers independently of collar derivatives, then fixes compact thresholds and offsets without circular dependence.
- **claim-hyperbolic-collar-control** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-collars)): For the fixed choices above, all sufficiently large $N$, and smooth solutions satisfying the floor condition $t\ge-\epsilon$, the first two stages have constants $c,C>0$, independent of $N$ and outer truncation, such that $$\frac c\tau\le\partial_\nu f\le\frac C\tau \quad\hbox{on black faces},\qquad \frac c\tau\le-\partial_\nu f\le\frac C\tau \quad\hbox{on white faces}.$$ In stage three, $\|\partial_\nu f\|\le C/\tau$. On each fixed compact set needed in Equation <a href="#eq:ah-offset-budget" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-offset-budget">[eq:ah-offset-budget]</a>, the physical heights satisfy $b_-\le h\le b_+$. On the fixed collars $\mathcal C$, for $\phi\ge0$, $$\label{eq:ah-polynomial-trace} \begin{split} \int_{\partial\Omega}\lambda L\phi &\le CN^m\int_{\mathcal C} u\{(1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\phi+\|d\phi\|_{A_\chi}\},\\ \int_{\partial\Omega}\phi &\le CN^m\int_{\mathcal C} \sqrt D\{(1+\sqrt{\mathcal T})\phi+\|d\phi\|_{A_\chi}\}. \end{split}$$ The finite exponent m is independent of $B_0,R,n_\infty$; fixed collar geometry affects the constant C.
  - Explanation: Transfers compact separation and signed slopes to the hyperbolic profiles and proves native-weight collar trace estimates with polynomial constants.
- **claim-hyperbolic-floor-separation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-floor)): A fixed sufficiently small $\delta_0>0$ and then a fixed finite integer $P_0$ can be chosen so that, for all sufficiently large N and all sufficiently distant truncations at fixed profiles, no smooth solution anywhere in the continuation can satisfy $t\ge-\epsilon$ and attain $t=-\epsilon$. Neither choice requires a fixed-profile Schauder constant.
  - Explanation: Chooses the floor coefficient and finite penalty exponent before fixed-profile regularity constants, excluding all floor contacts.
- **claim-hyperbolic-exterior-existence** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-ah-existence)): Choose $\delta_0,P_0$ as in Lemma <a href="#lem:ah-floor" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:ah-floor">79</a>. There is a fixed sufficiently large $B_0$, followed by a fixed exponent $a$ satisfying Equation <a href="#eq:ah-R-conditions" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-R-conditions">[eq:ah-R-conditions]</a>, such that for every sufficiently large $N$ the physical system has a smooth solution on the infinite exterior with $t\ge-\epsilon$. It is a smooth compact limit of solutions on sufficiently distant spherical truncations. At fixed profiles, $Z,t,D$, and all their derivatives on hyperbolic unit patches are bounded; derivatives of $f$ are bounded after multiplication by the local value of $\lambda$. These bounds are uniform in outer truncation. Moreover $R_{\widehat g}\ge-6$, and its inner boundary has strictly negative mean curvature.
  - Explanation: Obtains a complete physical solution by continuation and exhaustion, with fixed-profile local derivative bounds and the desired scalar and boundary curvature signs.
- **claim-hyperbolic-differentiated-end** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-ah-end)): For each fixed $N$, the solution of Proposition <a href="#prop:ah-existence" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="prop:ah-existence">80</a> satisfies $$\lambda f=O_j(r^{-\beta}),\qquad w=O_j(r^{-\beta}),\qquad Z-t=O_j(r^{-2\beta})$$ for every $j$, and $Z,t=O_j(r^{-\gamma})$ for every $\gamma<3$. Furthermore $$R_{\widehat g}+6=O_j(r^{-3-\delta}).$$ All four metric fluxes of $\widehat g$ exist. They satisfy Equation <a href="#eq:ah-alg-four-flux" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-alg-four-flux">[eq:ah-alg-four-flux]</a>, and the time component satisfies Equation <a href="#eq:ah-alg-time-flux" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:ah-alg-time-flux">[eq:ah-alg-time-flux]</a>.
  - Explanation: Proves all fixed-order physical end estimates, obtains scalar-curvature integrability, and invokes the exact metric-flux passage formulas.
- **claim-hyperbolic-vanishing-mass-loss** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-ah-mass-loss)): The profiles can be chosen in the stated order so that the physical solutions satisfy $$\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S_r}g(V_*,\nu_g)\,dA_g\ge-o_N(1).$$ Consequently $p_0(\widehat g)\le p_0(g)+o_N(1)$. The error depends on the fixed prepared data and tends to zero as $N\to\infty$.
  - Explanation: Estimates the primitive residual, penalty band, and boundary loss in the prescribed parameter order to control the time metric flux.
- **claim-lorentz-invariant-bound** (bound, [source](#stmt-thm-ah-invariant)): If the metric flux covector of the data in Theorem <a href="#thm:ah-component" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:ah-component">68</a> is future timelike, then $$m_{\rm AH}:=\sqrt{p_0^2-p_1^2-p_2^2-p_3^2} \ge \sqrt{\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{16\pi}} \left(1+\frac{A_{\min}(S;g)}{4\pi}\right).$$
  - Explanation: Balances only the original future-timelike metric covector by a spatial hyperbolic isometry and applies the fixed-chart component estimate.
- **claim-causal-killing-data** (construction, [source](#stmt-eq-causal-killing)): There are a smooth function $u$ and a smooth vector field $X$ on the one-sided manifold $\Omega$ with the following properties:* 1. *$u\geq \|X\|_g$ everywhere and $u>0$ in $\operatorname{int}\Omega$. For some $3/2<\beta<\min\{2,\tau\}$, $$u-V_0=O_{2,\alpha'}(r^{1-\beta}),\qquad X=O_{2,\alpha'}(r^{1-\beta}) \label{eq-end-normalization}$$ in background tensor norm, with $0<\alpha'<\alpha$.* 2. *In the interior, and by continuity at the boundary, $$\begin{aligned} \operatorname{sym}\nabla X&=-uK, \label{eq-shift}\\ \Delta u-3u&=-\operatorname{div}_g(K(X,\cdot)^\sharp),\label{eq-lapse}\\ \mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_g u&= u(\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_g+3g+(\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_gK)K-2K^2) -\mathcal L_XK+8\pi X_{(i}J_{j)}. \label{eq-full-lapse} \end{aligned}$$ Symmetrization includes averaging. Moreover $u\mu+J(X)=0$.* 3. *On $\mathbb R\times\operatorname{int}\Omega$, the metric $$\mathbf g=-u^2dt^2+ g_{ij}(dx^i+X^i\,dt)(dx^j+X^j\,dt) \label{eq-stationary-metric}$$ induces precisely the original $g$ and the original $K$ on $t=0$, with future normal $n=u^{-1}(\partial_t-X)$. Writing $\xi=\partial_t$ and $N=u^2-\|X\|_g^2$, one has $$\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_{\mathbf g}=-3\mathbf g+ 8\pi\mu u^{-2}\xi^\flat\otimes\xi^\flat,\qquad \mu N=0 . \label{eq-null-matter}$$* 4. *For the normal $\nu$ pointing into the exterior, $$X=u\nu,\qquad \partial_\nu u+K(X,\nu)=\kappa_h\quad\hbox{on }S. \label{eq-horizon-data}$$ Either $u>0$ on all of $S$, or $u=0$ on all of $S$.
  - Explanation: Produces smooth causal lapse and shift from equality of the original data, proves the full adjoint system, constructs the stationary metric, and determines the horizon surface gravity.
- **claim-area-envelope-derivative** (theorem, [source](#stmt-eq-area-envelope)): Let $g_s$ be a smooth metric path through $g$, with its first two parameter derivatives bounded relative to $g$, and with a common asymptotically hyperbolic $C^{2,\alpha'}$ bound of positive decay. Then, after restricting the parameter interval, the minimizing boundaries for $g_s$ lie in a common compact set. The family $\mathcal M$ is compact for indicator $L^1$ convergence and tangent-plane area-measure convergence. If $H=\dot g_0$, then $$\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right\|_{0+}A(s) =\min_{T\in\mathcal M}a'_T(H),\qquad a'_T(H)=\frac12\int_T\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}_T H\,dA_g. \label{eq-area-derivative}$$ Off the obstacle, minimizing boundaries that meet have the same tangent plane. This common plane is continuous on their union locally away from $S$.
  - Explanation: Establishes compactness and tangent-plane continuity of minimizing cuts and identifies the one-sided derivative of their area infimum.
- **claim-strict-conformal-direction** (construction, [source](#stmt-eq-strict-direction)): Choose $3/2<\beta<\min\{2,\tau\}$ and $0<\delta<\min\{1,2\beta-3\}$. There are smooth positive weights $w,w_2,D$, with $w=r^{-3-\delta}$, $w_2=r^{-\beta}$ on a far end and $D=O(r^{-\beta})$, $D\geq \|K\|$, and a smooth function $\phi=O_{2,\alpha'}(r^{-\beta})$, such that $$\begin{aligned} (-\Delta+3)\phi &=D\sqrt{w_2^2+\|d\phi\|^2}+w,& \partial_\nu\phi&=-1. \label{eq-strict-solve} \end{aligned}$$ It has finite fluxes against all four static potentials. In particular, $$(-\Delta+3)\phi\geq \|K\|\|d\phi\|+w,\qquad \frac{(-\Delta+3)\phi}{w}\longrightarrow1.$$ For $Q=(4\phi g,2\phi K)$, on the active set one has $$\mathcal C'_Q=8\big((3-\Delta)\phi+K(v,\nabla\phi)\big),\quad \mathcal C'_Q/w\longrightarrow8,\quad \theta'_Q=-4\ \hbox{on }S. \label{eq-strict-tests}$$
  - Explanation: Constructs a decaying conformal test direction giving a positive normalized active constraint derivative and a strictly negative boundary expansion derivative.
- **claim-positive-multiplier-separation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-eq-separation)): There are a probability measure $\omega$ on $\mathcal M$, a nonnegative finite measure $\eta$ on $S$, a nonnegative locally finite measure $\mathfrak L$ on $\mathcal Z$, and $z\geq0$, such that $w\mathfrak L$ is finite and $$16\pi p_0'-c\int_{\mathcal M}a'_T(H)\,d\omega(T) =\langle\mathcal C',\mathfrak L\rangle -\langle\theta',\eta\rangle+z\,a(H,P) \label{eq-multiplier-identity}$$ for every $(H,P)\in\mathcal V$.
  - Explanation: Separates admissible constraint variations from a strict improvement of the equality functional and obtains nonnegative multiplier measures.
- **claim-normal-slice-tests** (construction, [source](#stmt-eq-normal-tests)): For every $s\in C_c^\infty(\operatorname{int}\Omega)$, there are compact variations $(H_\epsilon,P_\epsilon)$ with $H_\epsilon=2sK$, supported in one fixed compact set, whose active-ray constraint derivatives tend uniformly to zero.
  - Explanation: Constructs compact normal slice variations whose active constraint derivatives vanish in the limit, including at vacuum rays.
- **claim-horizon-area-concentration** (theorem, [source](#stmt-eq-area-concentration)): The measure $\omega$ in Lemma <a href="#eq-separation" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq-separation">87</a> is concentrated on the single cut $S$.
  - Explanation: Concentrates the minimizing-area multiplier on the original horizon using normal tests, smooth MOTS comparison, and outermostness.
- **claim-local-smooth-causal-adjoint** (theorem, [source](#stmt-eq-local-adjoint)): Let $g,K$ be smooth on a connected open three-manifold and let $\Lambda_{\rm c}$ be constant. Suppose locally finite moment measures $u,X$ satisfy $u\geq\|X\|$, $u\mu_{\Lambda_{\rm c}}+J(X)=0$, and annihilate every compact variation of $16\pi(\mu_{\Lambda_{\rm c}}+J(v))$, including the isometric-vector correction <a href="#eq-vector-transport" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq-vector-transport">[eq-vector-transport]</a>. Then $u,X$ are smooth and $$\begin{aligned} \operatorname{sym}\nabla X&=-uK,\label{eq-general-shift}\\ \Delta u+\Lambda_{\rm c}u &=-\operatorname{div}_g(K(X,\cdot)^\sharp),\label{eq-general-lapse}\\ \mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}u &=u(\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}-\Lambda_{\rm c}g+\tau_KK-2K^2) -\mathcal L_XK+8\pi X_{(i}J_{j)},\qquad \tau_K=\mathop{\mathrm{tr}}K. \label{eq-general-full-lapse} \end{aligned}$$ Their full first jet satisfies a homogeneous linear first-order system with smooth coefficients depending on $g,K,\Lambda_{\rm c}$. A jet vanishing at one point vanishes everywhere. If the moments are nonzero, then $u>0$ everywhere.
  - Explanation: Upgrades moment measures to smooth adjoint fields, derives a homogeneous finite-type jet system, and obtains positivity of every nonzero causal lapse.
- **claim-adjoint-jet-compactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-eq-jet-compactness)): Suppose smooth coefficients in Lemma <a href="#eq-local-adjoint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="eq-local-adjoint">90</a> converge on compact subsets of a connected open manifold, and nonzero causal adjoints are defined on an exhaustion containing a fixed point $p$. Normalize their full first jets at $p$ to have norm one. A subsequence converges smoothly on compact sets to a nonzero causal adjoint for the limiting coefficients. The same conclusion holds for a parameter family on a fixed open manifold.
  - Explanation: Normalizes a nonzero adjoint jet and extracts a nonzero smooth causal limit using finite-type transport and local elliptic estimates.
- **claim-boundary-adjoint-normalization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-eq-normalization-lemma)): The moment fields extend smoothly to $S$, their original measure moments have no part supported on $S$, and they satisfy <a href="#eq-end-normalization" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq-end-normalization">[eq-end-normalization]</a>. In particular they are nonzero and their lapse is positive in the interior.
  - Explanation: Eliminates boundary measure atoms, extends the fields smoothly to the original boundary, and fixes their hyperbolic normalization using end tests.
- **claim-regular-static-quotient** (classification, [source](#stmt-geo-static-reduction)): Under these hypotheses, $N>0$ throughout $M$, and $M$ is simply connected.
