The fields $$h=g+N^{-1}X^\flat\otimes X^\flat, \qquad \lambda=\sqrt N,\qquad \mathcal A=N^{-1}X^\flat \label{geo-quotient-fields}$$ satisfy $h\geq g$ and $\,\mathrm d\mathcal A=0$, and there is a global smooth function $H$ on $M$ with $\,\mathrm dH=-\mathcal A$. They obey $$\Delta_h\lambda=3\lambda, \qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_h\lambda=\lambda(\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_h+3h), \qquad R_h=-6. \label{geo-static-equations}$$ Attaching $S$ in the regular boundary coordinates of Lemma <a href="#geo-boundary-collars" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="geo-boundary-collars">[geo-boundary-collars]</a> gives a smooth complete Riemannian manifold with compact connected nondegenerate boundary. Its underlying completion is homeomorphic to $\Omega$, and its boundary is identified diffeomorphically with $S$. On that boundary, $$h\|_{TS}=g\|_{TS},\qquad \mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_h(S)=\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_g(S),\qquad \lambda=0, \qquad \partial_{\nu_h}\lambda=\kappa_h, \qquad \mathrm{II}_h=0. \label{geo-quotient-boundary}$$ Moreover, in the original end chart, $$h-g=O_2(r^{-2\tau'}),\qquad \lambda-V_0=O_2(r^{1-\tau'}),\qquad \frac{\lambda}{V_0}\longrightarrow1. \label{geo-quotient-end}$$
  - Explanation: Obtains a globally timelike simply connected interior, a closed time connection, and a complete regular static quotient with inherited horizon and end data.
- **claim-timelike-end-boundary-collars** (bound, [source](#stmt-geo-positive-collars)): The end and a collar of $S$ in $M$ lie in $P$. In particular the interior zero set $Z=\{N=0\}\cap M$ is compact. If $u\|_S>0$, then $$\,\mathrm dN\|_S=2\kappa_h X^\flat\|_S, \qquad N=2\kappa_h u\|_S\,s+O(s^2), \label{geo-positive-boundary-jet}$$ where $s\geq0$ is $g$-normal distance into the domain. If $u\|_S=0$, there are smooth $a$ and $W$ in this collar such that $$u=sa,\qquad a\|_S=\kappa_h,\qquad X=s^2W, \qquad N=s^2\bigl(a^2-s^2\|W\|_g^2\bigr). \label{geo-zero-boundary-jet}$$
  - Explanation: Proves positivity of the stationary norm near the end and original boundary, leaving a compact possible interior null set and distinguishing both boundary lapse alternatives.
- **claim-killing-norm-twist-identities** (theorem, [source](#stmt-geo-killing-identities)): Let $D_{\alpha\beta}=\nabla^{\mathbf g}_\alpha\xi_\beta$, with the full Lorentzian contraction used in $\|D\|_{\mathbf g}^2$. On $M$, $$\frac1u\operatorname{div}_g(uC\,\,\mathrm dN) =6N-2\|D\|_{\mathbf g}^2. \label{geo-norm-identity}$$ On $P$, the antisymmetric contravariant tensor $$Q^{ij}=uN C^{ik}C^{j\ell}\mathcal F_{k\ell} \label{geo-Q}$$ satisfies $\nabla_iQ^{ij}=0$.
  - Explanation: Derives the stationary Killing-norm divergence identity and the divergence-free weighted twist tensor.
- **claim-transverse-logarithmic-energy** (bound, [source](#stmt-geo-logarithmic-energy)): On a neighborhood of $Z$, set $B=\|X\|_g$, $e=X/B$, and $T=e^\perp$. For each smooth compactly supported cutoff $\eta$ in that neighborhood, $$\sup_{\varepsilon>0} \int_M u\eta^2\frac{\|\,\mathrm dN\|_C^2}{(N+\varepsilon)^2}\,\mathrm dV_g<\infty. \label{geo-log-energy-bound}$$ In particular, $\,\mathrm d_T\log N$ is locally square integrable on the positive side up to $Z$: $$\int_P\eta^2\|\,\mathrm d_T\log N\|_g^2\,\mathrm dV_g<\infty. \label{geo-log-transverse}$$ No regularity or measure assumption on $Z$ is required.
  - Explanation: Controls logarithmic transverse energy up to an arbitrary compact null set without any assumed regularity or measure bound on that set.
- **claim-twist-vanishing** (theorem, [source](#stmt-geo-vanishing-twist)): The form $\mathcal A$ is closed on all of $P$.
  - Explanation: Removes null-set, boundary, and end cutoffs in the weighted twist identity to prove that the time connection is closed.
- **claim-static-timelike-connectedness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-geo-static-on-p)): Equations <a href="#geo-static-equations" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="geo-static-equations">[geo-static-equations]</a> hold on $P$, and $P$ is connected.
  - Explanation: Derives the static vacuum equations on the timelike region and excludes other components by the positive-lapse maximum principle.
- **claim-truncated-optical-completeness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-geo-optical-completeness)): Equip $P$ with the optical metric $k=\lambda^{-2}h$. All escape directions other than the ordinary end have infinite $k$-length. After truncating the ordinary end at a sufficiently large sphere, the resulting manifold with boundary is complete for its intrinsic optical distance. The same is true of each of its Riemannian covering spaces.
  - Explanation: Proves infinite optical distance to finite degenerations and original horizon approaches, including arbitrary tangential motion, and completeness after end truncation and lifting.
- **claim-null-index-obstruction** (theorem, [source](#stmt-geo-null-index-obstruction)): Let $(L,h,\lambda)$ satisfy the static equations in Equation <a href="#geo-static-equations" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="geo-static-equations">[geo-static-equations]</a>, with $\lambda>0$. Suppose that two compact boundary faces $\Sigma_0,\Sigma_1$ have positive $h$-mean curvature for the normals pointing out of $L$. There is no shortest optical path between these faces which is orthogonal at its endpoints and otherwise interior.
  - Explanation: Uses a negative null index variation to exclude a shortest interior optical path between compact faces with positive outward mean curvature.
- **claim-timelike-simple-connectivity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-geo-simple-connectivity)): The connected manifold $P$ is simply connected.
  - Explanation: Rules out multiple lifted end faces in the universal cover by optical properness and the null index obstruction.
- **claim-null-leaf-factorization** (theorem, [source](#stmt-geo-null-leaf-equations)): There is a neighborhood of $Z$ on which $X^\flat$ defines a smooth cooriented integrable plane field. In local foliated coordinates it has the form $$X^\flat=B_1\,\mathrm dy,\qquad B_1>0,\qquad g=q_y+D_1^2\,\mathrm dy^2,\qquad N=B_1a(y),\qquad a\geq0. \label{geo-null-foliation}$$ At any leaf in the relative boundary of $P$, one has $a=a'=0$. Put $b_1=\sqrt{B_1}$ and let $\mathcal K_y$ denote the Gaussian curvature of $q_y$. On such a boundary leaf, $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_{q_y}b_1=\tfrac12b_1(\mathcal K_y+3)q_y, \qquad \Delta_{q_y}(b_1^2)=6b_1^2-a''. \label{geo-boundary-leaf-system}$$
  - Explanation: Constructs a smooth cooriented foliation near the null set and derives the limiting static equations on boundary null leaves.
- **claim-fast-backward-transverse-arc** (construction, [source](#stmt-geo-flat-fast-arc)): Let $\phi_t$ be a smooth complete flow on a smooth Riemannian three-manifold $(M,g)$, and let $\mathcal K\subset M$ be a compact set invariant for all $t\in\mathbb R$. Suppose that a smooth nonvanishing one-form $\alpha$ is defined near $\mathcal K$, that $E=\ker\alpha$ is preserved by the differential of the flow along $\mathcal K$, and that, for every $p\in\mathcal K$, $t\geq0$, and $v\in E_p$, $$\label{geo-flat-rate-hypotheses} \lvert v\rvert_g\leq \lvert D\phi_t(p)v\rvert_g\leq e^t\lvert v\rvert_g, \qquad \alpha_{\phi_t(p)}\circ D\phi_t(p)=e^{2t}\alpha_p.$$ There are constants $\epsilon,C>0$ such that every $p\in\mathcal K$ admits a $C^1$ embedded arc $\gamma_p:(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\longrightarrow M$ with $$\label{geo-flat-arc-conclusion} \gamma_p(0)=p,\qquad \alpha_p(\gamma_p'(0))=1,\qquad d_g\bigl(\phi_{-t}(\gamma_p(\xi)),\phi_{-t}(p)\bigr) \leq C\lvert\xi\rvert e^{-3t/2}\quad(t\geq0).$$ By decreasing $\epsilon$, all the backward arcs can be kept in any prescribed neighborhood of $\mathcal K$. No regularity of the family $p\mapsto\gamma_p$ is asserted or needed.
  - Explanation: Builds an individual transverse contracting arc through each point of the compact invariant set using an invariant line and a contraction on backward orbit sequences.
- **claim-flat-null-leaf-exclusion** (theorem, [source](#stmt-geo-flat-exclusion)): Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth three-dimensional Riemannian manifold and let $N\in C^\infty(M)$ be nonnegative, with compact zero set $Z=\{N=0\}$. Put $P=\{N>0\}$, with boundary taken in $M$. Suppose a neighborhood $U$ of $Z$ carries a smooth nonvanishing one-form $\alpha$ defining a cooriented foliation by two-dimensional leaves. Assume that every sufficiently small foliated chart can be written as $$\label{geo-flat-factorization} \alpha=B\,\mathrm dy,\qquad B>0,\qquad N=B\,a(y),\qquad a\geq0,$$ with smooth coefficients. Let $q$ be the induced metric on a plaque $\Sigma=\{y=y_0\}\subset\partial P$, let $K_\Sigma$ be its Gaussian curvature, and put $b=\sqrt B$. Suppose the following leaf equations hold on every such plaque: $$\label{geo-flat-leaf-equations} \mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_\Sigma b=\tfrac12 b(K_\Sigma+3)q, \qquad \Delta_\Sigma(b^2)=6b^2-a''(y_0).$$ Then $\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_gN(p)\ne0$ for every $p\in\partial P$. Equivalently, every boundary zero in Equation <a href="#geo-flat-factorization" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="geo-flat-factorization">[geo-flat-factorization]</a> satisfies $a''(y_0)>0$.
  - Explanation: Excludes flat boundary null leaves by combining leafwise logistic dynamics, transverse contracting arcs, and incompatible backward bounds for the nonnegative norm.
- **claim-no-interior-null-set** (theorem, [source](#stmt-geo-no-null-set)): One has $Z=\varnothing$, and hence $P=M$.
  - Explanation: Turns nonflat null leaves into compact cooriented hypersurfaces and excludes them by their curvature and the topology of the simply connected timelike region.
- **claim-regular-static-boundary-collar** (construction, [source](#stmt-geo-static-collar)): The metric $h$ has the regular completion at $S$ stated in Equation <a href="#geo-quotient-boundary" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="geo-quotient-boundary">[geo-quotient-boundary]</a>. If $u\|_S=0$, its boundary structure is the original smooth boundary structure and $\mathcal A$ extends smoothly to $S$. If $u\|_S>0$, use $N$ as the original defining function and use $\lambda=\sqrt N$ as the quotient defining function. The quotient metric extends smoothly by reflection $\lambda\mapsto-\lambda$; its diagonal blocks are even and mixed block odd. In the original collar, $$\mathcal A=\frac1{2\kappa_h}\,\mathrm d\log N+\beta, \qquad \beta\text{ is smooth and closed up to }S. \label{geo-positive-A-collar}$$ In quotient normal distance $\rho$ from $S$, both cases satisfy $$h=\,\mathrm d\rho^2+q_0+O(\rho^2),\qquad \lambda=\kappa_h\rho+O(\rho^3), \label{geo-normal-boundary-jets}$$ with smooth one-sided coefficients. For a global primitive $\,\mathrm dH=-\mathcal A$, one has, respectively, $$H\text{ smooth up to }S, \qquad\text{or}\qquad H=-\frac1{2\kappa_h}\log N+B_0, \quad B_0\text{ smooth up to }S. \label{geo-time-collar}$$
  - Explanation: Completes the quotient smoothly at the original horizon and describes the time primitive in both boundary lapse alternatives, including the logarithmic term for positive boundary lapse.
- **claim-static-base-preserves-equality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-st-base-equality)): The metric $h$ has a smooth completion by the original boundary $S$, with its possibly changed transverse smooth coordinate. Its boundary data are $$h\|_{TS}=g\|_{TS},\qquad \lambda\|_S=0,\qquad \partial_{\nu_h}\lambda=\kappa,\qquad \mathrm{II}_h\|_S=0. \label{st-base-boundary}$$ The completed metric is complete, and $S$ is outer area-minimizing for $h$. Its four metric fluxes agree with those of $g$ in the original balanced chart. In particular, $$A_{\min,h}(S)=A_0, \qquad p(h)=(m,0,0,0), \qquad p_0(h)=\frac{r_h+r_h^3}{2}. \label{st-base-equality-data}$$ For some $\tau_1>3/2$, the end satisfies $$h-b=O_{2,\alpha_1}(r^{-\tau_1}),\qquad \lambda-V_0=O_{2,\alpha_1}(r^{1-\tau_1}),\qquad h-g=O_{2,\alpha_1}(r^{-2\tau_1}). \label{st-base-decay}$$ The last estimate is in physical tensor norm.
  - Explanation: Shows that the completed static base preserves the horizon area, outer area minimization, and all original balanced metric fluxes.
- **claim-regular-circle-bolt** (construction, [source](#stmt-st-bolt)): If the period of $\theta$ is $2\pi/\kappa$, collapsing its circles over $S$ extends <a href="#st-wick-metric" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="st-wick-metric">[st-wick-metric]</a> across a regular bolt. In polar Cartesian coordinates it is initially a $C^{2,\alpha}$ Einstein metric for every $0<\alpha<1$ and hence admits smooth Einstein coordinates across the bolt.
  - Explanation: Uses the surface-gravity period to extend the Riemannian Einstein metric across a regular bolt and then obtains smooth Einstein coordinates.
- **claim-weighted-einstein-gauge** (construction, [source](#stmt-st-weighted-gauge)): Let an Einstein metric $G$ on a tube end satisfy $G-G_0\in C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta}$ for some $\beta>3/2$. After a boundary-identity change of coordinates, its difference from $G_0$ belongs to $C^{k,\alpha_0}_{\delta}$ on a smaller end for every integer $k$ and every $0<\delta<3$. Here one can choose $\alpha_0>0$ below the original exponent. The coordinate change preserves circle translation and time reflection if $G$ does. In particular $G$ has an ordinary $C^{2,\alpha_2}$ conformal compactification for some $\alpha_2>0$.
  - Explanation: Constructs a symmetry-preserving harmonic gauge, improves weighted end decay, and obtains the preliminary ordinary conformal compactification.
- **claim-normalized-smooth-end** (construction, [source](#stmt-st-end-regularity)): There is a geodesic defining function $z$ for the conformal representative $d\theta^2+\sigma$ and a boundary-identity spatial collar identification in which $$\begin{split} h&=z^{-2}(dz^2+H(z)),\\ H(z)&=\sigma-\frac12z^2\sigma+z^3H_3+O(z^4),\\ z\lambda&=1+\frac14z^2+z^3\lambda_3+O(z^4). \end{split} \label{st-normalized-expansion}$$ All functions and tensor coefficients are smooth up to $z=0$. The full third coefficient of the compactified four-metric is $$G_3=H_3+2\lambda_3d\theta^2, \qquad \operatorname{tr}_{d\theta^2+\sigma}G_3=0, \qquad \operatorname{div}_{d\theta^2+\sigma}G_3=0. \label{st-free-tt-data}$$ The geodesic gauge preserves the circle factor and time reflection. The original and new defining radii are comparable, their collar maps extend to the same conformal boundary, and the resulting spatial mass comparison is covered by <a href="#lem:setup-mass-covariance" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:setup-mass-covariance">6</a>.
  - Explanation: Obtains a normalized smooth geodesic expansion preserving the circle symmetries, with constrained free coefficient and verified spatial mass comparison.
- **claim-static-heintze-karcher-deficit** (bound, [source](#stmt-hw-public-rigidity)): Let $(M^3,q,V)$ be a smooth static system satisfying $$\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_qV=V(\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_q+3q),\qquad \Delta_qV=3V,$$ with $V>0$ in the interior and connected compact nondegenerate horizon boundary $S=\{V=0\}$. Suppose a bounded smooth domain $\Omega$ has boundary $S\sqcup\Sigma$, where $\Sigma$ has strictly positive mean curvature $H$ toward the exterior of $\Omega$. Set $A=\mathop{\mathrm{Area}}_q(S)$ and $\kappa=\|\nabla V\|_S$. Then $$D=3A+2\pi\chi(S)>0,\qquad c=\frac{2A}{3D}>0.$$ The unique smooth solution of $$\label{hw-deficit-dirichlet} (\Delta_q-3)v=-1\quad\hbox{in }\Omega,\qquad v=c\quad\hbox{on }S,\qquad v=0\quad\hbox{on }\Sigma$$ satisfies $$\label{hw-static-deficit} \frac23\int_\Sigma\frac{V}{H} -\int_\Omega V-c\kappa A \geq\frac32\int_\Omega V\left\|\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}_qv-v(\mathop{\mathrm{Ric}}_q+3q)+\frac13q\right\|^2\geq0.$$ The measures in the surface and volume integrals are those of $q$.
  - Explanation: Proves positivity of the horizon denominator and bounds the static boundary-volume deficit below by a nonnegative interior tensor defect on a bounded domain.
- **claim-normalized-boundary-mass-integral** (theorem, [source](#stmt-hw-normalized-end)): In the normalized geodesic chart of Proposition <a href="#st-end-regularity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="st-end-regularity">110</a>, put $r=z^{-1}-z/4$ and $b=dr^2/(1+r^2)+r^2\sigma$. Then $$\label{hw-public-asymptotics} \sum_{j=0}^3\|\nabla_b^j(h-b)\|_b=O(r^{-3}),\qquad \lambda=\sqrt{1+r^2}+O_1(r^{-2}).$$ Let $\Sigma_z$ be a small positive constant-$z$ surface, with outward normal $\nu$ and mean curvature $H_z$. Then $$\label{hw-boundary-mass-limit} \lim_{z\downarrow0}\int_{\Sigma_z} \left(\frac{2\lambda}{H_z}-\partial_\nu\lambda\right) =-4\pi m_{\mathrm{AH}}.$$
  - Explanation: Evaluates the limiting mean-curvature and lapse boundary integral using the smooth normalized expansion and original balanced mass.
- **claim-global-static-model** (classification, [source](#stmt-hw-static-rigidity)): The completed static base is globally isometric, including its smooth boundary and its normalized lapse, to $$\label{hw-global-model} h=\frac{dr^2}{F_M(r)}+r^2\sigma,\qquad \lambda=\sqrt{F_M(r)},\qquad F_M(r)=1+r^2-\frac{2M}{r},\qquad r\geq r_h,$$ where the boundary is interpreted in spatial proper distance and $$\label{hw-actual-parameter} M=\frac{r_h+r_h^3}{2}=m_{\mathrm{AH}}>0.$$ The boundary is the entire model horizon sphere, and the unique end corresponds to $r\to\infty$.
  - Explanation: Identifies the complete equality base and its unrescaled lapse globally with the full Schwarzschild–anti-de Sitter exterior and its actual original metric mass.
- **claim-original-interior-graph** (construction, [source](#stmt-emb-interior)): There is a smooth function $H$ on $\operatorname{int}\Omega$ for which $$I(x)=\bigl(T=H(x),\,r(x),\,\omega(x)\bigr) \label{emb-graph}$$ is a spacelike embedding into the exterior with metric $$\mathbf g_M=-F(r)\,dT^2+\frac{dr^2}{F(r)}+r^2\sigma .$$ Its induced metric is exactly $g$, and its second fundamental form with the future normal is exactly $K$.
  - Explanation: Integrates the closed time connection and reconstructs an interior spacelike graph with precisely the original metric and future second fundamental form.
- **claim-original-horizon-extension** (construction, [source](#stmt-emb-horizon)): The graph <a href="#emb-graph" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="emb-graph">[emb-graph]</a> extends smoothly to the original closed manifold $\Omega$. If $u\|_S>0$, its boundary is a full smooth cross-section of $U=0$, $V>0$. If $u\|_S=0$, its boundary is the bifurcation sphere. In both cases the boundary map is a diffeomorphism onto that section.
  - Explanation: Extends the graph smoothly in the original boundary structure to a full future horizon section or the bifurcation sphere, with a boundary diffeomorphism.
- **claim-proper-original-embedding** (construction, [source](#stmt-emb-global)): The extended map $I$ is a smooth proper spacelike embedding of the original $(\Omega,g,K)$ into the smooth maximal Schwarzschild–AdS extension of parameter $M=m_{\mathrm{AH}}$. Its interior lies in one exterior, its boundary is the full future horizon section described in <a href="#emb-horizon" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="emb-horizon">115</a>, and its end reaches that exterior’s conformal infinity.
  - Explanation: Proves global properness, preservation of the future second form at the boundary, and arrival at the full conformal-infinity section.
- **claim-mass-matched-embedding-converse** (theorem, [source](#stmt-emb-converse)): Suppose the original data satisfy the connected horizon hypotheses of <a href="#def:setup-horizon" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="def:setup-horizon">8</a> and have the embedding required in <a href="#thm:main-rigidity" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:main-rigidity">2</a>, with its stipulated actual metric mass $M=m_{\mathrm{AH}}$. Then equality holds in the Penrose Inequality.
  - Explanation: Combines the full horizon-section area, assumed outer area minimization, and actual metric mass match to recover equality.
- **claim-nonstatic-equality-examples** (construction, [source](#stmt-emb-examples)): For every $M>0$, the static exterior with its bifurcation boundary attains equality. It also admits smooth compactly supported time graph perturbations with $K\not\equiv0$ which satisfy all the initial-data and connected horizon hypotheses and still attain equality with actual mass $m_{\mathrm{AH}}=M$.
  - Explanation: Constructs small compactly supported time graphs that retain all horizon hypotheses and the actual model mass while allowing nonzero second fundamental form.
- **claim-separated-face-linear-estimates** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-linear-separated-faces)): Let $U\Subset V$ be nested interior or boundary patches with uniformly controlled smooth geometry. Let $g$ be uniformly positive definite with uniformly controlled $C^2$ coordinate norms. Suppose that $u$ is smooth, $$Pu=-\Delta_g u+B\cdot du+cu=f, \qquad \\|B\\|_\infty+\\|c\\|_\infty\le K,$$ and that the physical boundary in $V$, if present, carries either $u=0$ or $\partial_{\nu_g}u=0$. For $1<p<\infty$, $$\\|u\\|_{W^{2,p}(U)} \le C\bigl(\\|f\\|_{L^p(V)}+\\|u\\|_{L^p(V)}\bigr).$$ The constant depends on the patch separation, ellipticity, principal coefficient modulus, and $K$, but not on a continuity modulus of $B$. If the coefficients and right side have uniform $C^{0,\gamma}$ bounds, the corresponding one-sided $C^{2,\gamma}$ estimates hold; Dirichlet data have norm $C^{2,\gamma}$ and Neumann data norm $C^{1,\gamma}$.* *On a compact connected smooth domain, let the Dirichlet and Neumann faces be disjoint unions of entire boundary components. With Hölder coefficients, $c\ge0$, and either $c\ge c_*>0$ or a nonempty Dirichlet face, $P$ is an isomorphism from the $C^{2,\gamma}$ space with homogeneous boundary conditions to $C^{0,\gamma}$. The Dirichlet Schauder a priori estimate also holds for a general uniformly elliptic principal matrix $A\in C^{0,\gamma}$, with Hölder lower-order coefficients. If $A\in C^{1,\gamma}$, the same isomorphism conclusion holds with all-Dirichlet boundary conditions.
  - Explanation: Provides local scalar Sobolev and one-sided Schauder estimates and the stated compact mixed or all-Dirichlet isomorphisms on disjoint boundary faces.

          "exact_quote": "An initial-data exterior is a connected orientable three-manifold $\\Omega$ with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S$, a Riemannian metric $g$, and a symmetric covariant tensor $K$. Outside a compact set there is a chart $(r_0,\\infty)\\times\\mathbb S^2$ with $$\\label{eq:setup-background}\n b=\\frac{dr^2}{1+r^2}+r^2\\sigma,\n \\qquad \\eta=\\operatorname{arsinh}r,$$ where $\\sigma$ is the unit round metric. For some $0<\\alpha<1$ and $3/2<\\tau<3$, assume $$\\label{eq:setup-decay}\n g-b\\in C^{2,\\alpha}_\\tau,\n \\qquad K\\in C^{1,\\alpha}_\\tau.$$ The space $C^{k,\\alpha}_\\tau$ controls $e^{\\tau\\eta}$ times the $b$-norm of every covariant derivative through order $k$, and the corresponding weighted Hölder seminorms on $b$-unit balls. The noncosmological constraint densities are $$\\label{eq:setup-constraints}\n 16\\pi\\mu=R_g+6+(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK)^2-\\lvert K\\rvert_g^2,\n \\qquad 8\\pi J=\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g\\bigl(K-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g\\bigr).$$ We require $$\\label{eq:setup-dec}\n \\mu\\ge\\lvert J\\rvert_g,\n \\qquad\n \\int_\\Omega\\sqrt{1+r^2}\n       \\bigl(\\mu+\\lvert J\\rvert_g+\\lvert K\\rvert_g^2\\bigr)\n       \\,\\mathrm dV_g<\\infty,$$ where the positive weight is extended smoothly over the compact part. No restriction is placed on the compact topology, the number of boundary components, or their genera.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.6"
        }
      ],

        "exact_quote": "Let $(\\Omega,g)$ be smooth up to its compact boundary.       "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-str-pde-fixed-height",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"thm:str-stress-dirichlet\" label=\"thm:str-stress-dirichlet\"></span> Let $(X,g)$ be a connected smooth complete three-dimensional exterior with compact smooth nonempty boundary, exactly one end, and a smooth metric up to its boundary. Let $H_{\\partial X}\\leq0$, for the normal pointing into $X$. Suppose that on the end, with $z=r^{-1}$, $$\\label{str-pde-prepared-end}\n g=z^{-2}\\bar g,\\qquad\n \\bar g=e^{4v}\\left(\\frac{dz^2}{1+z^2}+\\sigma\\right),\\qquad\n v=z^3v_3(\\omega)-d z^{3+\\delta}+O_\\infty(z^4),$$ where $v_3$ is smooth, $0<\\delta<1$, and the remainder and its tangential derivatives satisfy the indicated symbol estimates. For every $D>0$ there is a unique bounded weak solution $$\\label{str-pde-dirichlet}\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g\\left(t(|df|_g)\\frac{\\nabla_g f}{|df|_g}\\right)=0,\n \\qquad f|_{\\partial X}=D,\\qquad \\lim_{r\\to\\infty}f=0.$$ It satisfies $0<f<D$ in the interior, has bounded physical gradient, belongs to $C^{1,\\theta}$ on compact subsets including the finite boundary for some $\\theta>0$, and is smooth wherever $df\\ne0$. On a collar of conformal infinity it is noncritical and $$\\label{str-pde-end-expansion}\n\\begin{gathered}\n f=z C_f(\\omega)+R_f,\\qquad C_f\\in C^\\infty(\\mathbb S^2),\n \\qquad C_f>0,\\\\\n |(z\\partial_z)^j\\partial_\\omega^\\nu R_f|\n \\leq C_{j,\\nu}z^2\\quad(0\\leq j\\leq2).\n\\end{gathered}$$ The constants can depend on $D$ and the fixed geometry. In particular, $$\\label{str-pde-end-flux}\n \\begin{gathered}\n |df|_g=zC_f+O(z^2),\\qquad\n t(|df|_g)=z^2C_f^2+O(z^3),\\\\\n -\\lim_{r\\to\\infty}\\int_{\\{r=\\mathrm{const}\\}}\n t(|df|_g)\\left\\langle\\frac{\\nabla_g f}{|df|_g},\\nu_g\\right\\rangle\n dA_g=\\int_{\\mathbb S^2}C_f^2\\,dA_\\sigma .\n \\end{gathered}$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.6"
      },

        "exact_quote": "For sufficiently small $h>0$, choose a smooth $b_h$ equal to $1$ on $[0,h/2]$, equal to $b$ on $[2h,\\infty)$, and between $1$ and $2$ on the intervening interval. Define $t_h$ by $s t_h'/t_h=b_h$ and $t_h(2h)=t(2h)$. For each fixed $M<\\infty$, $$\\label{str-pde-regularized-structure}\n c_M(h+s)s\\leq t_h(s)\\leq C_M(h+s)s,\\qquad\n c_M(h+s)\\leq t_h'(s)\\leq C_M(h+s)\n \\quad(0\\leq s\\leq M).$$ Here $t_h(s)/s$ is constant near zero, so the regularized vector field is smooth at the zero covector. On interior unit patches for $h=0$, the estimate can be normalized to give $$\\label{str-pde-oscillation-gradient}\n \\sup_{B_{1/2}}|df|_g\\leq C\\operatorname{osc}_{B_1} f,$$ provided the same fixed extension and the same structural constants apply on the patch.         "anchor": "stmt-str-pde-linear-end-bounds",
        "exact_quote": "For the solution in Theorem <a href=\"#str-pde-fixed-height\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"str-pde-fixed-height\">13</a> there are $c,C,Q>0$ and a collar $0<z<z_0$ such that $$\\label{str-pde-linear-bounds}\n cz\\leq f\\leq Cz,\\qquad |df|_g\\leq Qz.$$ These constants can be chosen uniformly for a family whenever the coarse bounds $f\\leq C_0z^\\xi$, a positive lower bound on one fixed inner sphere, local physical gradient bounds, and the compact metric bounds used in the proof are uniform.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.6"
      },

          "anchor": "stmt-str-pde-fixed-height",
          "exact_quote": "<span id=\"thm:str-stress-dirichlet\" label=\"thm:str-stress-dirichlet\"></span> Let $(X,g)$ be a connected smooth complete three-dimensional exterior with compact smooth nonempty boundary, exactly one end, and a smooth metric up to its boundary. Let $H_{\\partial X}\\leq0$, for the normal pointing into $X$. Suppose that on the end, with $z=r^{-1}$, $$\\label{str-pde-prepared-end}\n g=z^{-2}\\bar g,\\qquad\n \\bar g=e^{4v}\\left(\\frac{dz^2}{1+z^2}+\\sigma\\right),\\qquad\n v=z^3v_3(\\omega)-d z^{3+\\delta}+O_\\infty(z^4),$$ where $v_3$ is smooth, $0<\\delta<1$, and the remainder and its tangential derivatives satisfy the indicated symbol estimates. For every $D>0$ there is a unique bounded weak solution $$\\label{str-pde-dirichlet}\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_g\\left(t(|df|_g)\\frac{\\nabla_g f}{|df|_g}\\right)=0,\n \\qquad f|_{\\partial X}=D,\\qquad \\lim_{r\\to\\infty}f=0.$$ It satisfies $0<f<D$ in the interior, has bounded physical gradient, belongs to $C^{1,\\theta}$ on compact subsets including the finite boundary for some $\\theta>0$, and is smooth wherever $df\\ne0$. On a collar of conformal infinity it is noncritical and $$\\label{str-pde-end-expansion}\n\\begin{gathered}\n f=z C_f(\\omega)+R_f,\\qquad C_f\\in C^\\infty(\\mathbb S^2),\n \\qquad C_f>0,\\\\\n |(z\\partial_z)^j\\partial_\\omega^\\nu R_f|\n \\leq C_{j,\\nu}z^2\\quad(0\\leq j\\leq2).\n\\end{gathered}$$ The constants can depend on $D$ and the fixed geometry. In particular, $$\\label{str-pde-end-flux}\n \\begin{gathered}\n |df|_g=zC_f+O(z^2),\\qquad\n t(|df|_g)=z^2C_f^2+O(z^3),\\\\\n -\\lim_{r\\to\\infty}\\int_{\\{r=\\mathrm{const}\\}}\n t(|df|_g)\\left\\langle\\frac{\\nabla_g f}{|df|_g},\\nu_g\\right\\rangle\n dA_g=\\int_{\\mathbb S^2}C_f^2\\,dA_\\sigma .\n \\end{gathered}$$",

        }

    {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-str-pde-growing-heights",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"lem:str-uniform-end\" label=\"lem:str-uniform-end\"></span> Let $g_i$ be smooth metrics on the same exterior, with $H_{\\partial X}(g_i)\\leq0$, converging smoothly on compact subsets to a smooth metric $g$. Suppose that each has the prepared end required for Theorem <a href=\"#str-pde-fixed-height\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"str-pde-fixed-height\">13</a>, and that for a common $\\beta>1$ and $M<\\infty$, $$\\label{str-pde-uniform-physical-metrics}\n \\sum_{j=0}^2|\\nabla_b^j(g_i-b)|_b\\leq Mz^\\beta$$ on a common end. Assume the compact metrics are uniformly positive definite. Let $D_i\\geq1$ be arbitrary finite heights and let $f_i$ be their solutions. Then on a common end collar there are constants $c,C,Q>0$, independent of $i,D_i$, such that $$\\label{str-pde-uniform-linear-bounds}\n cz\\leq f_i\\leq Cz,\\qquad |df_i|_{g_i}\\leq Qz.$$ For some $\\gamma>0$ the functions have uniform compact $C^{2,\\gamma}$ bounds on a common smaller collar, which is noncritical for every $f_i$. After extraction, they converge in $C^{2,\\gamma'}$ for $0<\\gamma'<\\gamma$ on a still smaller closed compact collar, and smoothly on interior compact subsets of that collar, to a solution for $g$. If $g$ has a smooth compactification in another defining function $\\rho$ comparable to $z$, the limiting solution is smooth there and has $f=\\rho C_\\infty+O(\\rho^2)$ with positive smooth $C_\\infty$.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.6"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-str-pde-growing-heights",
          "exact_quote": "<span id=\"lem:str-uniform-end\" label=\"lem:str-uniform-end\"></span> Let $g_i$ be smooth metrics on the same exterior, with $H_{\\partial X}(g_i)\\leq0$, converging smoothly on compact subsets to a smooth metric $g$. Suppose that each has the prepared end required for Theorem <a href=\"#str-pde-fixed-height\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"str-pde-fixed-height\">13</a>, and that for a common $\\beta>1$ and $M<\\infty$, $$\\label{str-pde-uniform-physical-metrics}\n \\sum_{j=0}^2|\\nabla_b^j(g_i-b)|_b\\leq Mz^\\beta$$ on a common end. Assume the compact metrics are uniformly positive definite. Let $D_i\\geq1$ be arbitrary finite heights and let $f_i$ be their solutions.         "exact_quote": "For a solution $f$ of the saturating equation, put $\\sigma=|df|$, $e=\\nabla f/|df|$ at noncritical points, and $k=(1-t(\\sigma)^{3/2})^{1/2}$. Define $$\\mathcal P_{ee}=2k,\\qquad\n \\mathcal P|_{e^\\perp}=\\frac{3+k^2}{2k}I,\\qquad\n \\mathcal P_{e\\perp}=0,\n \\qquad L=\\mathcal P-\\tfrac12(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_g\\mathcal P)g.\n \\label{eq:str-stress-definition}$$ At a critical point set $\\mathcal P=2g$ and $L=-g$. These fields are continuous, smooth away from the critical set, and satisfy $$\\operatorname{div}_g\\mathcal P=0,\n \\qquad (\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gL)^2-|L|_g^2=6,\n \\qquad L<0.\n \\label{eq:str-stress-identities}$$ If $K-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK)g\\geq0$, then $\\mathcal P:K\\leq0$. Therefore $(g,K+L)$ satisfies the flat-cosmological DEC whenever $(g,K)$ satisfies the $\\Lambda=-3$ DEC, with at least the original strict margin, and its future boundary expansion is strictly smaller.*\n\n*On any compact set where the DEC and expansion have strict margins, $\\mathcal P$ can be smoothed preserving those margins.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-str-bend-constraints",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"str-bc-constraints\" label=\"str-bc-constraints\"></span> Let $$q=F^{-1}ds^2+s^2\\gamma,\\qquad F>0,\\qquad n=\\sqrt F\\,\\partial_s.$$ Write the orthonormal blocks of a symmetric tensor $B$ as $$B_{nn}=-h,\\qquad B_{nT}=G,\\qquad B_T=-kI+U,\n \\qquad \\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_\\gamma U=0.$$ Here $G$ and $U$ are represented by a one-form and a symmetric tracefree two-tensor on the unit sphere. Put $\\mathcal H=R_q+(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_qB)^2-|B|_q^2$ and $\\mathcal D=\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_q(B-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_qB)q)$. Then $$R_q=\\frac{2(1-F)}{s^2}-\\frac{2\\partial_sF}{s}\n       -\\frac{2\\sqrt F}{s^2}\\Delta_\\gamma F^{-1/2}.\n \\label{str-bc-scalar}$$ In particular, if $F=1+s^2k^2-2m/s$, then $$\\mathcal H=\\frac{4\\partial_sm}{s^2}\n -\\frac{2\\sqrt F}{s^2}\\Delta_\\gamma F^{-1/2}\n +4k(h-k-s\\partial_sk)-2|G|^2-|U|^2.\n \\label{str-bc-hamiltonian}$$ For arbitrary $F$ the momentum components are $$\\begin{aligned}\n \\mathcal D_n&=\\frac{2\\sqrt F}{s}(k+s\\partial_sk-h)\n +\\frac{\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_\\gamma G-2G\\cdot\\nabla_\\gamma\\log\\sqrt F}{s},\n \\label{str-bc-momentum-normal}\\\\\n \\mathcal D_T&=\\sqrt F(\\partial_sG+3G/s)\n +\\frac{1}{s}\\bigl\\{\\nabla_\\gamma(h+k)\n -(h-k)\\nabla_\\gamma\\log\\sqrt F\\bigr\\}\\nonumber\\\\\n &\\hspace{12mm}+\\frac{1}{s}\\bigl\\{\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}_\\gamma U\n                    -U\\nabla_\\gamma\\log\\sqrt F\\bigr\\}.\n \\label{str-bc-momentum-tangent}\n\\end{aligned}$$",
        "source_id": "PM-260.6"
      },

      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-prop-str-af-bending",
        "exact_quote": "<span id=\"str-bc-bending\" label=\"str-bc-bending\"></span> Suppose $(\\Omega,g,B)$ is smooth, has one end, has strictly negative future boundary expansion, and satisfies $\\mathcal H_g-2|\\mathcal D_g|_g>0$ everywhere. Suppose its end is $g=e^{4v}b$, where $$v=r^{-3}v_3(\\omega)-d_0r^{-3-\\delta}+O_3(r^{-4}),\n \\qquad 0<\\delta<1,\\quad d_0>0,\n \\label{str-bc-prepared-v}$$ with smooth angular coefficients. Suppose also that on this end there are a positive smooth $C(\\omega)$ and a unit covector $e$ such that $$B=-g+\\frac{C^3}{r^3}\n       \\left(\\frac12g-\\frac32e\\otimes e\\right)+O_1(r^{-4}),\n \\qquad e\\otimes e=n_r^\\flat\\otimes n_r^\\flat+O_1(r^{-1}),\n \\label{str-bc-prepared-B}$$ where $n_r$ is the outward unit normal to the coordinate spheres. The scalar remainder has three symbol derivatives so that the change to the area coordinate has two controlled metric derivatives. The initial interpolation needs two derivatives of the metric error and one of the tensor error; the preparation in Lemma <a href=\"#lem:str-preparation\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:str-preparation\">11</a> supplies the stronger scalar expansion with all symbol derivatives.*\n\n\n\n\n\n*For every $\\varepsilon>0$ and every fixed compact subset there exist smooth data $(q_\\varepsilon,B_\\varepsilon)$ agreeing with $(g,B)$ on that subset and near the original boundary, such that $$\\begin{aligned}\n &q_\\varepsilon\\geq(1-\\varepsilon)g,\n \\label{str-bc-lower-comparison}\\\\\n &R_{q_\\varepsilon}+(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}B_\\varepsilon)^2-|B_\\varepsilon|^2\n -2|\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}(B_\\varepsilon-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}B_\\varepsilon)q_\\varepsilon)|\n \\geq c_\\varepsilon(1+s)^{-3-\\delta}>0,\n \\label{str-bc-strict-dec}\\\\\n &q_\\varepsilon-\\delta_{\\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_\\infty(s^{-1}),\\qquad\n R_{q_\\varepsilon}=O_\\infty(s^{-3-\\delta}),\\nonumber\\\\\n &B_\\varepsilon=O_\\infty(s^{-2}),\\qquad\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{q_\\varepsilon}B_\\varepsilon=0\n \\quad\\hbox{on the final end}.\n \\label{str-bc-af-bounds}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Its metric ADM energy satisfies $$\\fint_{\\mathbb S^2}(8v_3-C^3/2)\n \\leq E(q_\\varepsilon)\n \\leq\\fint_{\\mathbb S^2}(8v_3-C^3/2)+\\varepsilon.\n \\label{str-bc-energy}$$ Consequently its full-cut area infimum is at least $(1-\\varepsilon)A_g(S)$.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.6"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-prop-str-af-bending",
          "exact_quote": "<span id=\"str-bc-bending\" label=\"str-bc-bending\"></span> Suppose $(\\Omega,g,B)$ is smooth, has one end, has strictly negative future boundary expansion, and satisfies $\\mathcal H_g-2|\\mathcal D_g|_g>0$ everywhere. Suppose its end is $g=e^{4v}b$, where $$v=r^{-3}v_3(\\omega)-d_0r^{-3-\\delta}+O_3(r^{-4}),\n \\qquad 0<\\delta<1,\\quad d_0>0,\n \\label{str-bc-prepared-v}$$ with smooth angular coefficients. Suppose also that on this end there are a positive smooth $C(\\omega)$ and a unit covector $e$ such that $$B=-g+\\frac{C^3}{r^3}\n       \\left(\\frac12g-\\frac32e\\otimes e\\right)+O_1(r^{-4}),\n \\qquad e\\otimes e=n_r^\\flat\\otimes n_r^\\flat+O_1(r^{-1}),\n \\label{str-bc-prepared-B}$$ where $n_r$ is the outward unit normal to the coordinate spheres. The scalar remainder has three symbol derivatives so that the change to the area coordinate has two controlled metric derivatives. The initial interpolation needs two derivatives of the metric error and one of the tensor error; the preparation in Lemma <a href=\"#lem:str-preparation\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:str-preparation\">11</a> supplies the stronger scalar expansion with all symbol derivatives.*\n\n\n\n\n\n*For every $\\varepsilon>0$ and every fixed compact subset there exist smooth data $(q_\\varepsilon,B_\\varepsilon)$ agreeing with $(g,B)$ on that subset and near the original boundary, such that $$\\begin{aligned}\n &q_\\varepsilon\\geq(1-\\varepsilon)g,\n \\label{str-bc-lower-comparison}\\\\\n &R_{q_\\varepsilon}+(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}B_\\varepsilon)^2-|B_\\varepsilon|^2\n -2|\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}(B_\\varepsilon-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}B_\\varepsilon)q_\\varepsilon)|\n \\geq c_\\varepsilon(1+s)^{-3-\\delta}>0,\n \\label{str-bc-strict-dec}\\\\\n &q_\\varepsilon-\\delta_{\\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_\\infty(s^{-1}),\\qquad\n R_{q_\\varepsilon}=O_\\infty(s^{-3-\\delta}),\\nonumber\\\\\n &B_\\varepsilon=O_\\infty(s^{-2}),\\qquad\n \\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{q_\\varepsilon}B_\\varepsilon=0\n \\quad\\hbox{on the final end}.\n \\label{str-bc-af-bounds}\n\\end{aligned}$$ Its metric ADM energy satisfies $$\\fint_{\\mathbb S^2}(8v_3-C^3/2)\n \\leq E(q_\\varepsilon)\n \\leq\\fint_{\\mathbb S^2}(8v_3-C^3/2)+\\varepsilon.\n \\label{str-bc-energy}$$ Consequently its full-cut area infimum is at least $(1-\\varepsilon)A_g(S)$.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.6"

        "anchor": "stmt-thm-fl-deformation",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(\\Omega_{\\mathrm{orig}},q,B)$ be smooth three-dimensional initial data on a connected orientable manifold with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S_0$. Assume that the metric space including $S_0$ is complete and has exactly one asymptotically Euclidean end. On that end, in Euclidean coordinates of radius $r$, suppose that, for some $0<\\delta<1$, $$\\label{eq:fl-data-decay}\n q-\\delta_{\\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_\\infty(r^{-1}),\\qquad\n R_q=O_\\infty(r^{-3-\\delta}),\\qquad\n B=O_\\infty(r^{-2}),\\qquad \\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_qB=0.$$ Here $O_\\infty(r^{-a})$ includes all differentiated symbol estimates: each Euclidean derivative lowers the indicated order by one. Extend $r$ to a positive smooth function on the whole manifold. Suppose that there is $c_*>0$ such that $$\\label{eq:fl-strict-dec}\n R_q+(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_q B)^2-\\lvert B\\rvert_q^2\n -2\\bigl\\lvert\\operatorname{div}_q\n          \\bigl(B-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_qB)q\\bigr)\\bigr\\rvert_q\n \\ge c_*(1+r)^{-3-\\delta},$$ and that $H_q+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{S_0}B<0$ on every component of $S_0$, with the normal pointing into the exterior.*\n\n*For every connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary $D\\subset\\Omega_{\\mathrm{orig}}$, closed as a subset and with $\\operatorname{int}D\\subset\\operatorname{int}\\Omega_{\\mathrm{orig}}$, that contains the entire sufficiently distant end and whose *full compact intrinsic boundary* is smoothly embedded and two-sided, use that entire boundary as an enclosing cut. Allow coincidence with components of $S_0$, and allow $D=\\Omega_{\\mathrm{orig}}$, whose cut is $S_0$. Set $$A_*=\\inf_D\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_q(\\partial D).$$ Then the metric ADM energy satisfies $$E_q\\ge \\sqrt{\\frac{A_*}{16\\pi}}.$$ The boundary, the intermediate cuts, and the compact interior topology are otherwise unrestricted.",

      },

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-fl-mots-barriers",
        "exact_quote": "Let $(M,g,Q)$ be a smooth compact three-manifold with boundary $\\Gamma_-\\sqcup\\Gamma_+$. Every connected component of $M$ is required to meet $\\Gamma_+$. The outer part $\\Gamma_+$ has $\\Theta_Q>0$ with its normal out of $M$. The required inner part $\\Gamma_-$ may be empty; when present it has $\\Theta_Q<0$ with its normal into $M$.*\n\n*Consider all smooth bounding domains that contain a relative collar of $\\Gamma_-$, avoid $\\Gamma_+$, and whose free boundary has $\\Theta_Q\\le0$ with the normal out of the domain. If this collection is nonempty, the closure of its union has smooth compact embedded stable MOTS free frontier. It is itself the closure of a bounding domain and contains every domain in the collection. If $\\Gamma_-\\ne\\varnothing$, the strict inner and outer barriers give a nonempty smooth enclosing MOTS. Boundary parts and frontiers may be disconnected. No constraint or energy condition on $Q$ is required.",

      },

        "exact_quote": "Let $M$ be a smooth compact connected three-manifold with boundary $\\Gamma_-\\sqcup\\Gamma_+$, where $\\Gamma_+\\ne\\varnothing$. Let $E\\ne\\varnothing$ be closed, contain a relative collar of the required $\\Gamma_-$ if it is present, and have positive distance from $\\Gamma_+$. Suppose every exterior support of its interior frontier has $Q$-expansion at most $c$. If $$c'>c,\\qquad\n \\Theta_Q(\\Gamma_+)>c'$$ with the outward normal of $M$, then $E$ is strictly enclosed by a smooth bounding domain whose free frontier has expansion $c'$.         "exact_quote": "The thresholds and the prepared exterior above can be chosen so that both full threshold families are right-continuous at their chosen thresholds, the retained faces have disjoint collars as in Lemma <a href=\"#lem:fl-frontier-collars\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:fl-frontier-collars\">28</a>, and Equation <a href=\"#eq:fl-cut-inclusion\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:fl-cut-inclusion\">[eq:fl-cut-inclusion]</a> holds.     {
      "conclusion": {
        "anchor": "stmt-lem-fl-alg-floor-gauss",
        "exact_quote": "For a symmetric tensor $A$, define $$\\mathcal S(A)\n =\\frac14(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_\\perp A)^2-\\frac12|A_\\perp^{\\mathrm{tf}}|^2\n       +dA_{ee}\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_\\perp A-d|A_{e\\perp}|^2.$$ At an interior floor contact, $$\\frac12e^{4t}R_{\\hat g}\n \\le \\frac12R_g-v\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e,e)+\\mathcal S(H^f).\n \\label{eq:fl-alg-floor-gauss}$$ The expression $v\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_g(e,e)$ is interpreted as $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_g(w,w)$; all quantities have continuous, direction-independent values at $w=0$.",
        "source_id": "PM-260.6"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-reg-rank-one",
        "exact_quote": "Let $U$ be an interior coordinate ball or a smooth boundary half-ball, with a uniformly controlled $C^2$ metric $g$. In the boundary case assume that $z$ is constant on the face. At a zero of $\\nabla z$, an arbitrary measurable unit direction is allowed, provided Equation <a href=\"#reg-trace-equation\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"reg-trace-equation\">[reg-trace-equation]</a> holds with that choice. Assume $|\\nabla z|\\le L$ and $|G|\\le Q$. There are $\\alpha\\in(0,1)$, a uniform positive radius $r_0$, and $C$, depending only on $c_0$, the indicated geometry, and separation from the other faces of the patch, such that on a smaller patch $$\\|Dz\\|_{C^{0,\\alpha}}\\le C(L+Q),\\qquad\n \\int_{B_r(x)\\cap U}|\\mathop{\\mathrm{Hess}}z|^2\\,dV_g\n       \\le C(L+Q)^2r^{1+2\\alpha}\\quad(0<r\\le r_0).\n \\label{reg-main-estimates}$$ The constants $\\alpha,r_0,C$ do not depend on a modulus of continuity of $b$ or $G$.         "exact_quote": "Suppose $Z$ is locally Lipschitz, $|Z|\\le M$, and satisfies, in distributions on a ball in $\\mathbb R^3$, $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{div}}(aDZ+B)=e,\n \\qquad \\lambda I\\le a=a^T\\le\\Lambda I,\n \\qquad \\|B\\|_\\infty\\le B_0,\n \\label{reg-natural-equation}$$ where $a$ is measurable and $e$ is a signed Radon measure.         "anchor": "stmt-reg-coupled-bootstrap",
        "exact_quote": "Consider a family of smooth solutions $(f,Z)$ on smooth finite domains with uniformly controlled interior and boundary patches. Assume $|f|+|Df|+|Z|\\le M$ and the following structural bounds, uniformly in the family:*\n\n1.  *The $f$-equation has the form of Equation <a href=\"#reg-trace-equation\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"reg-trace-equation\">[reg-trace-equation]</a>, with $b\\ge c_0>0$ and bounded $G$. Its actual matrix and source are smooth functions of $(x,Z,f,Df)$ on the bounded variable range, including at $Df=0$. The value of $f$ on each boundary face is constant.*\n\n\n2.  *After multiplication by the coordinate volume density, the $Z$-equation is $$\\partial_i\\bigl(a^{ij}(x,Z,f,Df)\\partial_jZ\n                               +B^i(x,Z,f,Df)\\bigr)=Q,\n     \\qquad\n     |Q|\\le C(1+|DZ|^2+|D^2f|^2),\n     \\label{reg-coupled-Z}$$ where $a$ is symmetric and uniformly elliptic and $B$ is bounded. The functions $a,B$ and $Q$, as a function also of $(DZ,D^2f)$, are smooth on the ranges on which they are used.*\n\n\n3.  *Each boundary component for $Z$ has either constant Dirichlet data, or bounded total conormal flux. In the latter case its equation can also be solved as $$\\partial_\\nu Z=H(x,Z,f,Df),\n     \\label{reg-normal-data}$$ where $H$ is smooth on the bounded variable range. These faces are disjoint and have no edges where the type of data changes.*\n\n*Assume that the derivatives of the displayed smooth functions and the geometry are bounded to the order needed for each stated estimate. Then $f$ and $Z$ have uniform local classical estimates of every such finite order, including at the boundary.       ],
      "exact_statement": "The flat exterior of Theorem <a href=\"#thm:fl-deformation\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:fl-deformation\">25</a> satisfies $$E_g\\ge\\sqrt{\\frac{A_*}{16\\pi}}.$$",
      "explanation": "Applies the Riemannian Penrose theorem to the full outermost minimal comparison frontier and passes ordered numerical limits.",
      "fidelity": "PENDING",
      "hypotheses": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-thm-fl-deformation",
          "exact_quote": "Let $(\\Omega_{\\mathrm{orig}},q,B)$ be smooth three-dimensional initial data on a connected orientable manifold with nonempty compact smooth boundary $S_0$. Assume that the metric space including $S_0$ is complete and has exactly one asymptotically Euclidean end. On that end, in Euclidean coordinates of radius $r$, suppose that, for some $0<\\delta<1$, $$\\label{eq:fl-data-decay}\n q-\\delta_{\\mathrm{Eucl}}=O_\\infty(r^{-1}),\\qquad\n R_q=O_\\infty(r^{-3-\\delta}),\\qquad\n B=O_\\infty(r^{-2}),\\qquad \\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_qB=0.$$ Here $O_\\infty(r^{-a})$ includes all differentiated symbol estimates: each Euclidean derivative lowers the indicated order by one. Extend $r$ to a positive smooth function on the whole manifold. Suppose that there is $c_*>0$ such that $$\\label{eq:fl-strict-dec}\n R_q+(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_q B)^2-\\lvert B\\rvert_q^2\n -2\\bigl\\lvert\\operatorname{div}_q\n          \\bigl(B-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_qB)q\\bigr)\\bigr\\rvert_q\n \\ge c_*(1+r)^{-3-\\delta},$$ and that $H_q+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{S_0}B<0$ on every component of $S_0$, with the normal pointing into the exterior.*\n\n*For every connected smooth codimension-zero submanifold-with-boundary $D\\subset\\Omega_{\\mathrm{orig}}$, closed as a subset and with $\\operatorname{int}D\\subset\\operatorname{int}\\Omega_{\\mathrm{orig}}$, that contains the entire sufficiently distant end and whose *full compact intrinsic boundary* is smoothly embedded and two-sided, use that entire boundary as an enclosing cut. Allow coincidence with components of $S_0$, and allow $D=\\Omega_{\\mathrm{orig}}$, whose cut is $S_0$. Set $$A_*=\\inf_D\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_q(\\partial D).$$ Then the metric ADM energy satisfies $$E_q\\ge \\sqrt{\\frac{A_*}{16\\pi}}.$$ The boundary, the intermediate cuts, and the compact interior topology are otherwise unrestricted.",
          "source_id": "PM-260.6"
        }
      ],
      "id": "claim-flat-mass-completion",
      "kind": "bound",
      "quantifiers": [],
      "statement_anchor": "stmt-thm-fc-mass-completion"
    },

      "exact_statement": "Suppose the lapse is the profile defined in Section <a href=\"#subsec:ah-profiles\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"subsec:ah-profiles\">7.2</a>; in particular $l_0(t,x)=e^{n(x)t}$ for $t\\le0$ and $l_0(0,x)=1$.       "conclusion": {

        "exact_quote": "For the fixed choices above, all sufficiently large $N$, and smooth solutions satisfying the floor condition $t\\ge-\\epsilon$, the first two stages have constants $c,C>0$, independent of $N$ and outer truncation, such that $$\\frac c\\tau\\le\\partial_\\nu f\\le\\frac C\\tau\n \\quad\\hbox{on black faces},\\qquad\n \\frac c\\tau\\le-\\partial_\\nu f\\le\\frac C\\tau\n \\quad\\hbox{on white faces}.$$ In stage three, $|\\partial_\\nu f|\\le C/\\tau$.         "anchor": "stmt-eq-causal-killing",
        "exact_quote": "There are a smooth function $u$ and a smooth vector field $X$ on the one-sided manifold $\\Omega$ with the following properties:*\n\n\n1.  *$u\\geq |X|_g$ everywhere and $u>0$ in $\\operatorname{int}\\Omega$. For some $3/2<\\beta<\\min\\{2,\\tau\\}$, $$u-V_0=O_{2,\\alpha'}(r^{1-\\beta}),\\qquad\n     X=O_{2,\\alpha'}(r^{1-\\beta})\n     \\label{eq-end-normalization}$$ in background tensor norm, with $0<\\alpha'<\\alpha$.*\n\n\n\n2.  *In the interior, and by continuity at the boundary, $$\\begin{aligned}\n     \\operatorname{sym}\\nabla X&=-uK, \\label{eq-shift}\\\\\n     \\Delta u-3u&=-\\operatorname{div}_g(K(X,\\cdot)^\\sharp),\\label{eq-lapse}\\\\\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{Hess}}_g u&=\n     u(\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_g+3g+(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK)K-2K^2)\n     -\\mathcal L_XK+8\\pi X_{(i}J_{j)}. \\label{eq-full-lapse}\n    \\end{aligned}$$ Symmetrization includes averaging. Moreover $u\\mu+J(X)=0$.*\n\n\n\n3.  *On $\\mathbb R\\times\\operatorname{int}\\Omega$, the metric $$\\mathbf g=-u^2dt^2+\n     g_{ij}(dx^i+X^i\\,dt)(dx^j+X^j\\,dt)\n     \\label{eq-stationary-metric}$$ induces precisely the original $g$ and the original $K$ on $t=0$, with future normal $n=u^{-1}(\\partial_t-X)$. Writing $\\xi=\\partial_t$ and $N=u^2-|X|_g^2$, one has $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_{\\mathbf g}=-3\\mathbf g+\n           8\\pi\\mu u^{-2}\\xi^\\flat\\otimes\\xi^\\flat,\\qquad\n     \\mu N=0 .\n     \\label{eq-null-matter}$$*\n\n4.  *For the normal $\\nu$ pointing into the exterior, $$X=u\\nu,\\qquad\n     \\partial_\\nu u+K(X,\\nu)=\\kappa_h\\quad\\hbox{on }S.\n     \\label{eq-horizon-data}$$ Either $u>0$ on all of $S$, or $u=0$ on all of $S$.",

      },

        {

          "exact_quote": "There are a smooth function $u$ and a smooth vector field $X$ on the one-sided manifold $\\Omega$ with the following properties:*\n\n\n1.  *$u\\geq |X|_g$ everywhere and $u>0$ in $\\operatorname{int}\\Omega$.           "anchor": "eq-section",
          "exact_quote": "We assume equality in Theorem <a href=\"#thm:ah-invariant\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"thm:ah-invariant\">83</a>. All variations below are variations of the original pair $(g,K)$ on the original manifold $\\Omega$. Nearby data need satisfy only the hypotheses of the numerical inequality; their boundaries need not remain outermost or area-minimizing. Here $\\tau$ again denotes the original asymptotically hyperbolic decay exponent in Definition <a href=\"#def:setup-data\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:setup-data\">3</a>.\n\n\n\nChoose a balanced spatial chart, so that $p_0=m_{\\rm AH}$ and $p_i=0$ at the data under consideration. Put $$A=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_g(S),\\qquad r_h=\\sqrt{A/(4\\pi)},\\qquad\n c=16\\pi\\frac{d}{dA}\\frac{r_h+r_h^3}{2}\n   =\\frac{1+3r_h^2}{r_h},\\qquad \\kappa_h=\\frac c2 .\n \\label{eq-area-constant}$$ The fixed-chart time component is a supporting functional for the Lorentz norm of a future-timelike covector. Consequently the numerical inequality gives, for all sufficiently small admissible variations, $$p_0(g_s)\\ \\geq\\ m_{\\rm AH}(g_s)\\\n \\geq\\ \\frac{r_{A(s)}+r_{A(s)}^3}{2},\n \\qquad r_{A(s)}=\\sqrt{A(s)/(4\\pi)}.\n \\label{eq-supporting-inequality}$$ Here $A(s)$ is the minimum full enclosing area for $g_s$. Equality holds throughout at $s=0$. Only spatial chart covariance is used in choosing the balanced chart.\n\n\n<div id=\"eq-causal-killing\" class=\"theorem\">\n\n**Theorem 84** (Causal Killing data produced by equality). *There are a smooth function $u$ and a smooth vector field $X$ on the one-sided manifold $\\Omega$ with the following properties:*\n\n\n1.  *$u\\geq |X|_g$ everywhere and $u>0$ in $\\operatorname{int}\\Omega$. For some $3/2<\\beta<\\min\\{2,\\tau\\}$, $$u-V_0=O_{2,\\alpha'}(r^{1-\\beta}),\\qquad\n     X=O_{2,\\alpha'}(r^{1-\\beta})\n     \\label{eq-end-normalization}$$ in background tensor norm, with $0<\\alpha'<\\alpha$.*\n\n\n\n2.  *In the interior, and by continuity at the boundary, $$\\begin{aligned}\n     \\operatorname{sym}\\nabla X&=-uK, \\label{eq-shift}\\\\\n     \\Delta u-3u&=-\\operatorname{div}_g(K(X,\\cdot)^\\sharp),\\label{eq-lapse}\\\\\n     \\mathop{\\mathrm{Hess}}_g u&=\n     u(\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_g+3g+(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_gK)K-2K^2)\n     -\\mathcal L_XK+8\\pi X_{(i}J_{j)}. \\label{eq-full-lapse}\n    \\end{aligned}$$ Symmetrization includes averaging. Moreover $u\\mu+J(X)=0$.*\n\n\n\n3.  *On $\\mathbb R\\times\\operatorname{int}\\Omega$, the metric $$\\mathbf g=-u^2dt^2+\n     g_{ij}(dx^i+X^i\\,dt)(dx^j+X^j\\,dt)\n     \\label{eq-stationary-metric}$$ induces precisely the original $g$ and the original $K$ on $t=0$, with future normal $n=u^{-1}(\\partial_t-X)$. Writing $\\xi=\\partial_t$ and $N=u^2-|X|_g^2$, one has $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{Ric}}_{\\mathbf g}=-3\\mathbf g+\n           8\\pi\\mu u^{-2}\\xi^\\flat\\otimes\\xi^\\flat,\\qquad\n     \\mu N=0 .\n     \\label{eq-null-matter}$$*\n\n4.  *For the normal $\\nu$ pointing into the exterior, $$X=u\\nu,\\qquad\n     \\partial_\\nu u+K(X,\\nu)=\\kappa_h\\quad\\hbox{on }S.\n     \\label{eq-horizon-data}$$ Either $u>0$ on all of $S$, or $u=0$ on all of $S$.*\n\n</div>\n\nWe prove the theorem without assuming a stationary development. The Lorentzian metric in its statement will be constructed only after the multiplier fields have been obtained and shown to be smooth and positive.\n\n\n#### The envelope derivative for full enclosing area\n\nExtend $g$ smoothly across a short collar of $S$, and fix the entire inner side of that collar as an obstacle. This auxiliary extension is used only for perimeter minimization. It is not required to satisfy constraints. Minimize among bounded filled sets containing the obstacle, taking perimeter in the extended open collar and the original exterior. Thus the obstacle itself has boundary $S$ and perimeter $\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_g(S)$: the convention does not erase $S$ when the exterior competitor is $D=\\Omega$.\n\nBounded complementary pockets can be filled. Their removal from the exterior component cannot increase perimeter, and any nonempty pocket of a regular minimizer would contribute removable positive perimeter. The remaining complement is the connected exterior containing the end. Conversely, every full cut in the original definition gives a filled competitor in this formulation. A compact $C^{1,1}$ obstacle boundary can be pushed slightly into the exterior by a collar vector field and then smoothed in graph charts. These operations preserve separation and make its areas converge. The perimeter infimum therefore equals the infimum over the smooth full cuts of Definition <a href=\"#def:setup-cut\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"def:setup-cut\">4</a>.\n\nLet $\\mathcal M$ denote the family of boundaries attaining this perimeter infimum for $g$.\n\n\n<div id=\"eq-area-envelope\" class=\"lemma\">\n\n\n**Lemma 85** (Compact minimizing family and area derivative). *Let $g_s$ be a smooth metric path through $g$, with its first two parameter derivatives bounded relative to $g$, and with a common asymptotically hyperbolic $C^{2,\\alpha'}$ bound of positive decay. Then, after restricting the parameter interval, the minimizing boundaries for $g_s$ lie in a common compact set. The family $\\mathcal M$ is compact for indicator $L^1$ convergence and tangent-plane area-measure convergence. If $H=\\dot g_0$, then $$\\left.\\frac{d}{ds}\\right|_{0+}A(s)\n   =\\min_{T\\in\\mathcal M}a'_T(H),\\qquad\n a'_T(H)=\\frac12\\int_T\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_T H\\,dA_g.\n \\label{eq-area-derivative}$$ Off the obstacle, minimizing boundaries that meet have the same tangent plane. This common plane is continuous on their union locally away from $S$.*\n\n</div>\n\n<details id=\"proof-stmt-eq-area-envelope\"><summary>Proof of stmt-eq-area-envelope</summary>\n\n*Proof.* Large coordinate spheres have mean curvature $2+o(1)$, uniformly for these paths. Fix a radius beyond which this mean curvature is positive and the obstacle is absent. On a larger compact truncation, the direct method for perimeter gives an obstacle minimizer. Its boundary cannot have a maximal radius in the strictly mean-convex region: at a free maximum it is minimal and lies on the inner side of a strictly mean-convex coordinate sphere, in contradiction with the local comparison principle. Contact with the outer truncation can likewise be moved inward to lower area. Thus every such minimizer lies inside the same fixed radius. Truncations containing any prescribed smooth competitor show that their minimum is the full infimum.\n\nThe local obstacle regularity theorem (Huisken and Ilmanen 2001, Regularity Theorem 1.3(iii)) [[huiskenilmanen2001](#ref-huiskenilmanen2001)] applies here to pure perimeter, a smooth obstacle, a smooth metric and ambient dimension three. It gives $C^{1,1}$ boundaries and smooth minimal free parts. Part (iii) is used for this individual regularity. For a fixed $0<\\alpha_0\\le1/2$, the local $C^{1,\\alpha_0}$ estimates in Part (ii) are uniform: the obstacle bounds and positive metric $C^1$ bounds are uniform for the family $g_s$.\n\nOnly away from $S$ do we need density estimates. Here is a local proof with uniform constants. In a sufficiently small ball centered at a boundary point, compare a minimizing set $E$ with $E\\setminus B_\\rho$ and $E\\cup B_\\rho$, filling any unnecessary pockets afterwards. The ball misses the obstacle. For $f(\\rho)=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Vol}}(E\\cap B_\\rho)$, minimality and coarea give, for almost every $\\rho$, $$P(E;B_\\rho)\\le f'(\\rho),\\qquad\n P(E\\cap B_\\rho)\\le2f'(\\rho).$$ Uniform local isoperimetry implies $f'(\\rho)\\ge c f(\\rho)^{2/3}$, hence $f(\\rho)\\ge c\\rho^3$. The same argument applies to the complement. Relative isoperimetry then gives $P(E;B_\\rho)\\ge c\\rho^2$; the comparison above and the uniform sphere-area bound give $P(E;B_\\rho)\\le C\\rho^2$. These constants are uniform on compact sets disjoint from $S$. Perimeter compactness now gives subsequential indicator convergence. Lower semicontinuity, together with testing a fixed minimizer, gives convergence of perimeters, including for varying metrics.\n\nHere is the measure-continuity detail needed for differentiation. In a fixed orthonormal frame let $D\\chi_{E_j}$ be the vector normal measures. Their weak convergence and convergence of total variations imply weak convergence of their variation measures: any weak limit dominates $|D\\chi_E|$, and equality of total masses eliminates the excess. Approximate the limiting unit normal in the square-integral norm of this measure by continuous vector fields. For such a field $v$, expand $$\\int|\\nu_j-v|^2\\,d|D\\chi_{E_j}|\n =\\int(1+|v|^2)\\,d|D\\chi_{E_j}|\n       -2\\int v\\cdot dD\\chi_{E_j}.$$ Both terms converge. Continuous approximation and uniform continuity then give convergence for every continuous function of position and unit normal, and hence for functions of the unoriented tangent plane. A partition of unity proves the assertion globally. Uniform metric convergence converts varying-metric perimeters to this fixed-metric argument.\n\nOn every rectifiable cut of bounded area, the area-element expansion is uniform: $$\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_{g_s}(T)=\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_g(T)+s\\,a'_T(H)\n                      +O(s^2)\\mathop{\\mathrm{Area}}_g(T).\n \\label{eq-area-taylor}$$ A fixed minimizing cut gives the upper one-sided bound in <a href=\"#eq-area-derivative\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq-area-derivative\">[eq-area-derivative]</a>. For the lower bound take minimizers $T_s$ for $g_s$, pass along any sequence $s\\downarrow0$ to a member $T\\in\\mathcal M$, and use $$\\frac{A(s)-A(0)}s\n   \\geq a'_{T_s}(H)+O(s)\\longrightarrow a'_T(H).$$ Compactness and continuity of $a'_T(H)$ prove the formula.\n\nFinally, the union and intersection of two filled minimizing sets remain obstacle competitors. Perimeter submodularity gives $$P(E_1\\cup E_2)+P(E_1\\cap E_2)\n       \\leq P(E_1)+P(E_2)=2A.$$ Both terms on the left are at least $A$, so both are minimizers. Different tangent planes at an intersection would give a corner in one of them, contradicting interior regularity. To check continuity on the union, take points on a sequence of minimizers converging away from the obstacle. The two phase-volume density bounds prevent disappearance of the limiting point under indicator convergence, so it lies on a limiting minimizer. The uniform local $C^{1,\\alpha_0}$ estimates and strict perimeter convergence then give tangent-plane convergence there. The common-plane property makes this independent of the chosen sequence. ◻\n\n</details>\n\n\n#### A strict direction and the asymptotic test generators\n\n\nUse the fixed unit ball bundle $$\\mathcal B=\\{(x,v):x\\in\\Omega,\\ |v|_g\\leq1\\},\\qquad\n \\mathcal C(x,v)=16\\pi(\\mu(x)+J_x(v)),\n \\qquad \\mathcal Z=\\{\\mathcal C=0\\}.$$ In a metric variation $g_s(\\cdot,\\cdot)=g(A_s\\cdot,\\cdot)$, transport $v$ by $v_s=A_s^{-1/2}v$. This preserves its length and gives $$\\dot v_0=-\\tfrac12 H^\\sharp v.\n \\label{eq-vector-transport}$$ Every constraint derivative below includes this term.\n\n\n<div id=\"eq-strict-direction\" class=\"lemma\">\n\n\n**Lemma 86** (Strict conformal direction). *Choose $3/2<\\beta<\\min\\{2,\\tau\\}$ and $0<\\delta<\\min\\{1,2\\beta-3\\}$. There are smooth positive weights $w,w_2,D$, with $w=r^{-3-\\delta}$, $w_2=r^{-\\beta}$ on a far end and $D=O(r^{-\\beta})$, $D\\geq |K|$, and a smooth function $\\phi=O_{2,\\alpha'}(r^{-\\beta})$, such that $$\\begin{aligned}\n (-\\Delta+3)\\phi\n   &=D\\sqrt{w_2^2+|d\\phi|^2}+w,&\n \\partial_\\nu\\phi&=-1. \\label{eq-strict-solve}\n\\end{aligned}$$ It has finite fluxes against all four static potentials. In particular, $$(-\\Delta+3)\\phi\\geq |K||d\\phi|+w,\\qquad\n \\frac{(-\\Delta+3)\\phi}{w}\\longrightarrow1.$$ For $Q=(4\\phi g,2\\phi K)$, on the active set one has $$\\mathcal C'_Q=8\\big((3-\\Delta)\\phi+K(v,\\nabla\\phi)\\big),\\quad\n \\mathcal C'_Q/w\\longrightarrow8,\\quad\n \\theta'_Q=-4\\ \\hbox{on }S.\n \\label{eq-strict-tests}$$*\n\n</div>\n\n<details id=\"proof-stmt-eq-strict-direction\"><summary>Proof of stmt-eq-strict-direction</summary>\n\n*Proof.* Solve <a href=\"#eq-strict-solve\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq-strict-solve\">[eq-strict-solve]</a> on spherical truncations with outer Dirichlet value zero. Continue both the source and the inner Neumann value from zero. The gradient term can be written $b\\cdot d\\phi+f$, where $$|b|\\leq D,\\qquad 0\\leq f\\leq Dw_2+w .$$ The operator is consequently $-\\Delta-b\\cdot\\nabla+3$. A fixed collar function supplies the prescribed outward Neumann derivative, which is $+1$; adding a sufficiently large constant dominates its bounded compactly supported derivatives and the source. The maximum principle gives a bound independent of the truncation and continuation parameter. Beyond a fixed sphere, $$(3-\\Delta_b)r^{-\\beta}\n   =(3-\\beta)(1+\\beta)r^{-\\beta}+O(r^{-\\beta-2}).$$ The decaying drift and metric errors preserve its positive leading coefficient. Comparison with a multiple of this function, using the already bounded value on the fixed sphere and zero outer data, gives $|\\phi|\\leq C r^{-\\beta}$.\n\nLemma <a href=\"#lem:linear-separated-faces\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"lem:linear-separated-faces\">119</a>, followed by Sobolev embedding and the one-sided Schauder estimate, gives the same weighted bound through two derivatives. At the fixed inner face use the corresponding Neumann estimates. The linearized equation has bounded drift, zeroth-order coefficient $3$, homogeneous Neumann data at the inner face and homogeneous Dirichlet data at the outer face. Its kernel is zero by the maximum principle, so the usual elliptic Fredholm alternative makes it invertible. The a priori estimates close the method of continuity on each truncation. Exhaustion and local compactness then produce the asserted decaying solution, smooth on compact sets including the one-sided boundary.\n\nThe additional source is $O(r^{-2\\beta})=o(w)$, proving the ratio claim. Replacing $\\Delta_g$ by $\\Delta_b$ costs $O(r^{-\\tau-\\beta})$. Both this error and $r^{-2\\beta}$ have finite integrals with weight $V_0\\,dV_b$, as does $w$. The scalar linearization identity $$\\operatorname{div}_b\\mathbb U(V,4\\phi b)\n       =8V(3-\\Delta_b)\\phi,\\qquad \\mathop{\\mathrm{Hess}}_bV=Vb,$$ therefore proves existence of all the conformal fluxes. Replacing $b$ by $g$ in $4\\phi b$ costs order $r^{-\\tau-\\beta}$, beyond the mass order.\n\nFor the exact conformal transformation $g_s=e^{4s\\phi}g$, $K_s=e^{2s\\phi}K$, direct differentiation gives $$\\mathcal C'_Q=-4\\phi\\mathcal C+\n       8((3-\\Delta)\\phi+K(v,\\nabla\\phi)).$$ The first term vanishes on $\\mathcal Z$. The expansion transforms as $\\theta_s=e^{-2s\\phi}(\\theta+4s\\partial_\\nu\\phi)$; since $\\theta=0$ on $S$, its derivative is $-4$. ◻\n\n</details>\n\nIn addition to $Q$, take all compact variations, including arbitrary one-sided jets at $S$, and the following end variations, cut off near the compact interior:\n\n1.  $(4\\psi g,2\\psi K)$, where $\\psi=r^{-3}f(\\omega)$ and $f\\in C^\\infty(\\mathbb S^2)$;\n\n2.  pure tensor variations $(0,P)$ whose trace reversal with respect to $b$ has only mixed block $$(P-(\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_bP)b)_{\\nu_b A}=r^{-3}W_A(\\omega)$$ in radial and spherical orthonormal scaling, for arbitrary smooth one-forms $W$ on $\\mathbb S^2$.\n\nTheir constraint derivatives are $o(w)$ on the active rays. Indeed the conformal radial indicial term cancels, leaving an $O(r^{-5})$ background scalar term and products with the decaying original coefficients. For the mixed block, its radial derivative is $-3(V_0/r)r^{-3}W_A$; the sphere connection terms give $+3(V_0/r)r^{-3}W_A$. Thus its tangential background divergence is zero, while its normal divergence is $r^{-4}\\operatorname{div}_\\sigma W$. Metric and tensor errors cost $O(r^{-3-\\tau})$. The choice $\\delta<1$ proves the assertion.\n\nLet $\\mathcal V$ be the real linear space generated by these tests. The coefficient $a(H,P)$ of $Q$ is well defined even if $\\mathcal Z$ is compact. Indeed, on the full unit ball bundle, $\\mathcal C=O(r^{-\\tau})$, uniformly in $v$, and the conformal identity in the preceding proof gives $$\\frac{\\mathcal C'_Q}{w}\n =8+o(1)-\\frac{4\\phi\\mathcal C}{w}=8+o(1).$$ Here $\\tau+\\beta>2\\beta>3+\\delta$, so the last term tends to zero. The other generators have normalized full-ball derivative tending to zero by the same end calculations (and compact variations vanish there). Applying these limits to any linear relation among the generators forces the coefficient of $Q$ to vanish. The active-ray statement is its restriction when active rays exist.\n\n\n#### Positive separation of the active constraints\n\n\n<div id=\"eq-separation\" class=\"lemma\">\n\n\n**Lemma 87** (Multiplier identity). *There are a probability measure $\\omega$ on $\\mathcal M$, a nonnegative finite measure $\\eta$ on $S$, a nonnegative locally finite measure $\\mathfrak L$ on $\\mathcal Z$, and $z\\geq0$, such that $w\\mathfrak L$ is finite and $$16\\pi p_0'-c\\int_{\\mathcal M}a'_T(H)\\,d\\omega(T)\n =\\langle\\mathcal C',\\mathfrak L\\rangle\n       -\\langle\\theta',\\eta\\rangle+z\\,a(H,P)\n \\label{eq-multiplier-identity}$$ for every $(H,P)\\in\\mathcal V$.*\n\n</div>\n\n<details id=\"proof-stmt-eq-separation\"><summary>Proof of stmt-eq-separation</summary>\n\n\n*Proof.* Compactify $\\mathcal Z$ by one point, collapsing all rays whose base points escape compact sets; if it was compact, add an isolated point. The ball fibers are compact. The functions $\\mathcal C'/w$ extend continuously with value $8a(H,P)$. On the disjoint compact union of this space, $S$, and $\\mathcal M$, consider the linear test map $$(H,P)\\longmapsto\n \\big(\\mathcal C'/w,\\ -\\theta',\\\n          c\\,a'_T(H)-16\\pi p_0'\\big).\n \\label{eq-test-map}$$ Lemma <a href=\"#eq-area-envelope\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"eq-area-envelope\">85</a> supplies continuity on the last piece.\n\nSuppose its image contained a function positive everywhere. Write its direction as $aQ+(H_0,P_0)$. Positivity at the additional point gives $a>0$. Realize the direction by $$g_s=e^{4as\\phi}(g+sH_0),\\qquad\n K_s=e^{2as\\phi}(K+sP_0).$$ These metrics remain positive and uniformly comparable to $g$. On the far end, retain the nonnegative background constraint with its positive conformal scaling factor. The remaining terms have the following bounds, uniformly over the unit ball: $$\\begin{array}{c|c}\n \\text{term}&\\text{size}\\\\ \\hline\n \\text{strict conformal gain}&8asw\\\\\n \\text{non-strict linear changes}&s\\,o(w)\\\\\n \\text{new quadratic and cross terms}&O(s^2w).\n \\end{array}$$ For clarity, the non-strict end metric and tensor tests are $O(r^{-3})$, their background constraint terms are $O(r^{-4})+O(r^{-3-\\tau})$, and their products with the strict direction are $O(r^{-3-\\beta})$. The strict direction’s own quadratic errors are $O(r^{-2\\beta})$. All are controlled by $w$. Applying the exact conformal law after the intermediate variation gives these bounds without differentiating the nonnegative original constraint into an uncontrolled error. One may compose the two isometries of unit balls in this calculation: at an active unit ray a difference of isometric identifications is tangent to the unit sphere and is annihilated by $J$; at a vacuum ray $J=0$.\n\nOn the remaining compact ball bundle, positivity of the derivative on the closed active set persists on a neighborhood of it. The original constraint has a positive minimum on the compact complement. Taylor’s formula thus gives the DEC for sufficiently small $s>0$ everywhere. The boundary has strictly negative future expansion. The same estimates are integrable with weight $V_0$, and the flux divergence identity proves differentiability of all four fluxes. The covector remains future timelike by continuity. Thus <a href=\"#eq-supporting-inequality\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq-supporting-inequality\">[eq-supporting-inequality]</a> applies to this path.\n\nPositivity on $\\mathcal M$, however, says $$c\\min_{T\\in\\mathcal M}a'_T(H)-16\\pi p'_0>0.$$ By Lemma <a href=\"#eq-area-envelope\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"eq-area-envelope\">85</a> and <a href=\"#eq-area-constant\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq-area-constant\">[eq-area-constant]</a>, the right derivative at zero of the difference in <a href=\"#eq-supporting-inequality\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq-supporting-inequality\">[eq-supporting-inequality]</a> is negative. That difference is initially zero and is nonnegative for $s>0$, a contradiction.\n\nThe image of <a href=\"#eq-test-map\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq-test-map\">[eq-test-map]</a> is therefore disjoint from the open positive cone of continuous functions. Hahn–Banach separation gives a nonzero continuous functional, nonnegative on nonnegative functions and annihilating this linear image. The Riesz Representation Theorem gives finite nonnegative measures on its three compact pieces. The objective piece has positive mass: otherwise evaluation on $Q$, strictly positive on both other pieces, would contradict annihilation. Normalize that mass to one. Divide the finite measure on finite active rays by $w$ and call it $\\mathfrak L$; absorb eight times the end-point atom into $z$. Rearranging the identity gives <a href=\"#eq-multiplier-identity\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq-multiplier-identity\">[eq-multiplier-identity]</a>. ◻\n\n</details>\n\nDefine the first moments, initially as measures with the fixed-volume distribution convention, by $$\\langle u,f\\rangle=\\int f(x)\\,d\\mathfrak L(x,v),\\qquad\n \\langle X,\\alpha\\rangle=\\int\\alpha_x(v)\\,d\\mathfrak L(x,v).$$ Positivity and activity give $$u\\geq |X|_g,\\qquad u\\mu+J(X)=0\n \\label{eq-measure-complementarity}$$ as measure identities and inequalities.\n\n\n#### Removing the interior area multipliers\n\n\n<div id=\"eq-normal-tests\" class=\"lemma\">\n\n**Lemma 88** (Normal slice tests). *For every $s\\in C_c^\\infty(\\operatorname{int}\\Omega)$, there are compact variations $(H_\\epsilon,P_\\epsilon)$ with $H_\\epsilon=2sK$, supported in one fixed compact set, whose active-ray constraint derivatives tend uniformly to zero.*\n\n</div>\n\n<details id=\"proof-stmt-eq-normal-tests\"><summary>Proof of stmt-eq-normal-tests</summary>\n\n*Proof.* On a compact neighborhood of the support, choose a Gaussian Lorentzian collar $$\\mathbf g_\\epsilon=-dt^2+g_\\epsilon(t),\\qquad\n g_\\epsilon(0)=g,\\quad \\partial_tg_\\epsilon(0)=2K.$$ Prescribe its second time jets so that $$\\frac1{8\\pi}(G_{\\mathbf g_\\epsilon}-3\\mathbf g_\\epsilon)_{ij}\n       =D_{\\epsilon,ij},\\qquad\n D_\\epsilon=\\frac{J\\otimes J}{\\mu+\\epsilon}\n \\quad\\hbox{at }t=0.$$ The spatial Einstein tensor depends on the freely chosen normal derivative of $K$ by a nonzero multiple of trace reversal. In dimension three trace reversal has eigenvalues $1$ and $-2$; it is invertible. The remaining terms are fixed spatial jets. Thus these smooth second jets can be prescribed, and a quadratic time extension with a cutoff realizes a smooth Lorentzian metric on a sufficiently short collar. The normal and mixed components of the displayed tensor are $\\mu,J$, by the constraints.\n\nSet $D=J\\otimes J/\\mu$ where $\\mu>0$, and set it to zero at vacuum. The DEC gives $$|D_\\epsilon|\\leq\\mu,\\qquad\n |\\nabla D_\\epsilon|\\leq2|\\nabla J|+|\\nabla\\mu|.$$ At a zero of the smooth nonnegative function $\\mu$, its differential vanishes; $|J_i|\\leq\\mu$ then gives $dJ_i=0$ there also. The displayed derivative bound proves that $D$ is $C^1$ across vacuum with zero derivative there. Splitting any compact set into $\\{\\mu\\geq\\delta\\}$ and $\\{\\mu<\\delta\\}$ proves $D_\\epsilon\\to D$ in $C^1$.\n\nVary the slice by graphs $t=a s(x)$, differentiating at $a=0$. The metric derivative is $2sK$. At a nonvacuum active ray, $\\mu=|J|$, $v=-J^\\sharp/\\mu$, and $\\zeta=n+v$ is null. The limiting prescribed stress has the form $$\\mu^{-1}\\gamma\\otimes\\gamma,\\qquad\n \\gamma(n)=\\mu,\\quad\\gamma|_{T\\Omega}=J,\\quad\\gamma(\\zeta)=0.$$ The covector $\\gamma$ is nonnegative on future causal vectors. Parallel transport $\\zeta$ in any spatial direction using the spacetime connection. Its contraction with $\\gamma$ is nonnegative and has a zero, so its derivative there is zero. Consequently the spatial covariant derivatives of the limiting stress, contracted in one slot with $\\zeta$, vanish.\n\nLet $T_\\epsilon=(G_{\\mathbf g_\\epsilon}-3\\mathbf g_\\epsilon)/(8\\pi)$. Contracted Bianchi, before taking the limit, gives $$(\\nabla_nT_\\epsilon)(n,\\zeta)\n       =\\sum_i(\\nabla_{e_i}T_\\epsilon)(e_i,\\zeta).$$ The right side tends to zero by the compact $C^1$ convergence just proved. Thus the required normal derivative of the constraint combination tends to zero too. Differentiating its arguments causes no additional limiting term: the first argument is paired against a tensor with $\\zeta$ in its kernel, and the second argument remains null; at activity $\\gamma$ is proportional to $\\zeta^\\flat$, so nullity kills its differentiated contraction. At vacuum the tensor and its spatial derivatives vanish, and Bianchi gives the same conclusion for every vector in the closed unit ball. All expressions use only the fixed compact jets and $D_\\epsilon,\\nabla D_\\epsilon$; the convergence is uniform, including near vacuum. ◻\n\n</details>\n\n\n<div id=\"eq-area-concentration\" class=\"lemma\">\n\n**Lemma 89** (Concentration on the original horizon). *The measure $\\omega$ in Lemma <a href=\"#eq-separation\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"eq-separation\">87</a> is concentrated on the single cut $S$.*\n\n</div>\n\n<details id=\"proof-stmt-eq-area-concentration\"><summary>Proof of stmt-eq-area-concentration</summary>\n\n*Proof.* Apply Lemma <a href=\"#eq-normal-tests\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"eq-normal-tests\">88</a> in <a href=\"#eq-multiplier-identity\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq-multiplier-identity\">[eq-multiplier-identity]</a>. Mass, expansion and end-point terms are zero. The constraint measure is finite over the fixed compact support, so the limit gives $$\\int_{\\mathcal M}\\int_T s\\,\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_TK\\,dA_g\\,d\\omega(T)=0\n       \\qquad(s\\in C_c^\\infty(\\operatorname{int}\\Omega)).$$ Off $S$, form the positive aggregate area measure $\\mathfrak b=\\int_{\\mathcal M}dA_T\\,d\\omega(T)$. Lemma <a href=\"#eq-area-envelope\" data-reference-type=\"ref\" data-reference=\"eq-area-envelope\">85</a> makes $F(x)=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_{\\Pi(x)}K(x)$, for the common tangent plane $\\Pi(x)$, a single continuous function on the union of the cuts locally away from $S$. The last identity is $F\\mathfrak b=0$. Fubini on a countable compact exhaustion shows that, for $\\omega$-almost every cut, $\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_TK=0$ almost everywhere off $S$. Such a cut is smooth minimal there, so continuity gives $H_T=\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_TK=0$ throughout its free part.\n\nAt contact, write the cut and $S$ as $C^{1,1}$ graphs with the same orientation. Their second derivatives agree almost everywhere on the coincidence set: apply twice the fact that the derivative of a Lipschitz function vanishing on a measurable set is zero almost everywhere on that set. The cut therefore solves $H_T+\\mathop{\\mathrm{tr}}_TK=0$ almost everywhere across contact as well as away from it. This is a uniformly elliptic quasilinear graph equation.
